- Players can log out of all devices on Roblox by going to Settings > Security > Where You're Logged In and selecting Log Out of All Other Sessions.
- Roblox lets players review active sessions, check device details and locations, and remotely remove individual devices from their account.
- Logging out does not delete Robux, avatar items, game progress, or friends list, as all the data remains saved to the account.
Whether you forgot to log out on a shared school computer, handed your tablet to a friend, or suspect someone else has access to your profile, knowing how to sign out of all devices on Roblox is the fastest way to secure your account.
Thanks to Roblox’s Session Management feature, you do not need physical access to those other devices to kick them off. In this updated guide on how to log out of Roblox, we will walk you through clearing every active login across PC, Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Android in just a few clicks.
How to Sign Out of All Devices on Roblox at Once
To clear every active remote login at once, you need to use the Security tab inside your Roblox account settings. It is available in the section where you can verify age in Roblox. You can do this from either a computer browser or the mobile app.
How to Log Out of Roblox PC (Web Browser and Desktop App)
If you are on a Windows PC or Mac, follow these steps to sign out of Roblox PC across all your other devices linked sessions:
- Head over to the official Roblox website or open the Roblox Desktop app and log into your account.
- Click the Gear icon in the top-right corner of the screen and select Settings from the dropdown menu.
- Click on the Security tab in the left-hand sidebar menu.
- Scroll down until you see the Where you’re logged in section.
- Click the Log Out of All Other Sessions button located at the very bottom of the list.
- Click Log Out on the pop-up prompt to confirm.
How to Sign Out of All Devices on Roblox Mobile (iOS and Android)
If you don’t have a computer nearby or your Roblox account is hacked, there are some ways to log out from your phone. Here is how to sign out of all devices on Roblox mobile:
- Open the Roblox app on your iPhone, iPad, or Android device.
- Tap the More icon (the three dots) in the bottom-right navigation bar.
- Scroll down and tap Settings (the gear icon).
- Select Security from the settings list.
- Swipe down to the Where you’re logged in section to view all active devices.
- Tap Log Out of All Other Sessions at the bottom of the screen, then tap Log Out again on the confirmation window.
What Does Log Out of All Other Sessions on Roblox Mean?
If you are searching for the ‘Log out of all Other Sessions Roblox meaning’, read below before clicking the button to make sure it won’t mess up your current game.
When you select ‘Log Out of All Other Sessions’, Roblox immediately terminates every active login across all other phones, tablets, consoles, and computers except the exact device and browser/app you are currently using.
- You will stay signed in on the screen in front of you.
- Anyone else logged into your account or any old session left open on a library, school, or friend’s device will be instantly kicked back to the login screen.
How to Check All Logged-in Devices on Roblox (And Remove One Device)
Sometimes you don’t want to sign out of everything. You just want to check if an unfamiliar device is lurking on your account. If you are wondering how to check all logged-in devices on Roblox, the Session Management tool gives you all the options.
Reviewing Your Active Sessions
When you go to Settings > Security > Where you’re logged in, Roblox displays a consolidated list of every active session. For each login, you can see:
- Device Type & App/Browser: Whether the login is on an Android phone, iPad, Windows PC, or a specific web browser.
- Approximate Location: The city and region where the login occurred.
- Last Active Timestamp: The exact date and time that the device last interacted with Roblox. (Note: Older inactive logins with incomplete data may occasionally display as “Unknown”).
How to Kick a Single Device Off Your Account
If you spot one suspicious location or a specific friend’s device, you don’t have to reset every device you own. Here is how to remove a single session:
- Go to Settings > Security and scroll to Where you’re logged in.
- Click or tap on the specific session you do not recognize.
- Review the device name, location, and timestamp.
- Select Log out of session to disconnect that single device immediately.
How to Log Out of Roblox on Phone, iPad, or Android (Single Device)
If you are only trying to sign out of the device in your hand just to get rid of issues like Roblox error 262, you just need the standard Log Out button.
How to Log Out of Roblox on Phone (Android and iOS)
Whether you want to log out of Roblox on iPhone or Android phones, the steps in the mobile app are identical:
- Launch the Roblox mobile app and tap the More (three dots) button at the bottom of the screen.
- Scroll all the way to the bottom of the menu.
- Tap Log Out, then confirm by tapping Log Out again (make sure your email or phone number is linked first so you don’t get locked out).
How to Log Out of Roblox on iPad
If you play on an Apple tablet, here is how to sign out of Roblox on iPad:
- Open the Roblox app on your iPad and tap the More (three dots) icon in the bottom navigation bar (or left sidebar in landscape mode).
- Scroll down to the bottom of the page and tap Log Out.
- Confirm the prompt to sign out of that iPad only.
Sign Out Tips for PC Players on Roblox
If you only want to sign out of your current computer browser, click the Gear icon in the top-right corner of the Roblox website and click Log Out.
If you are constantly logging out and back in on PC just to swap between a main and an alt account, consider using separate browser profiles. You can also use a dedicated Roblox account manager like BetterLauncher so you don’t get stuck in a log-out loop.
That is how you can sign out of all devices on Roblox or just log out from a single session. Done with checking the session, you can also check your Roblox playtime here.
Can you log someone out of your Roblox account?
Yes, you can easily log someone else out of your Roblox account remotely. Go to Settings > Security > Where you’re logged in, tap on the person’s device, and select Log out of session.
How do I log out of my Roblox account on my phone?
To log out on your phone, open the Roblox app, tap the More (three dots) icon in the bottom-right corner, scroll to the very bottom of the menu, and tap Log Out.
Do I lose everything if I log out of Roblox?
No, you will not lose your Robux, avatar items, game progress, or friends list when you log out of Roblox. All of your data is saved to your Roblox account in the cloud.
Why do I keep getting logged out of Roblox automatically?
If Roblox keeps logging you out unexpectedly, it is usually caused by clearing your browser cookies, playing in an incognito/private window, or an expired login session.

A video is going viral on social media, where a young man is heard saying in Bangla, “We won’t allow any Hindutva aggression or Indian aggression in Jagannath University.”
The video wad shared by X handle Voice of BD Hindus (@HinduUnityBD) on November 7 with the claim that Muslim students of Jagannath University in Bangladesh had declared Diwali as a form of Hindutva aggression. (Archive)
🚨 BREAKING : Jamaat Student leaders at Jagannath University have declared Diwali a form of “Hindutva aggression” and “Indian aggression,”
announcing that they will not allow Diwali celebrations to take place on campus. But they can celebrate EID. A Hindu Zamindar Built Jagannath University.
— Voice Of BD Hindus 🇧🇩 (@HinduUnityBD) November 7, 2026
In the 25-second-long clip, the man states, “We won’t allow any Hindutva aggression or Indian aggression in Jagannath University. This university is situated in a country of 92% Muslims, and the university claims that it runs by nurturing the culture, ethics and heritage of the Muslims. If anyone wants to make things work differently, the people of Bangladesh will give a befitting reply. Inshallah”.
The video was also shared by X user Monica Verma with the claim that “Muslim Students in Bangladesh are calling Deepawali celebrations as “Hindu aggression” warning the Hindu students of consequences if they celebrate it.”
Muslim Students in Bangladesh are calling Deepawali celebrations as “Hindu aggression” warning the Hindu students of consequences if they celebrate it.
Indian as well as the global Media will never show you this side of the F*cked Up Bangladeshi Gen Z. https://t.co/wij366yQtp
— Monica Verma (@TrulyMonica) November 7, 2026
Several other prominent Indian social media users shared the same video with similar claims.
Fact Check
To verify the authenticity of the claim, we conducted a reverse image search using key frames from the video in question.
This led us to a video published by Bangladesh-based media outlet ‘Desh Somoy News’. The video is identical to the one currently going viral and was published on October 16 in connection with the beef festival controversy at Jagannath University in Dhaka.
The controversy at Dhaka’s Jagannath University began on October 12, when students of the department of Islamic history and culture organised a beef feast near the university’s central temple. Hindu students objected to the proximity of the cooking arrangements to the temple and the alleged use of temple bricks to build a makeshift stove. Protests followed, triggering a wider dispute on campus.
On October 14, the university administration issued a notice prohibiting animal slaughter on campus, prompting further student protests.
Protesting against the administrative decision, students led by the Jagannath University Central Student’s Union organized a rally in the campus on October 14 itself, and held an impromptu press conference after the protest rally. The video in question is from that press conference.
Bangladesh-based online news portal Bd24report covered the press conference on its Facebook page on October 14. The live video is 17 minutes long, and from 5:13 minute mark, the press conference can be seen. At the 8:39-minute mark, the social work secretary of the Student’s Union, Mustafizur Rahaman, addresses the press. Rahaman is the same person seen speaking in the viral video.
Rahaman spoke from 8:50 till 10:56 minute mark, and the viral snippet is from 10:22 till 10:47. There was no mention of Diwali in the entire programme. The students spoke in protest against the University administration’s decision to ban animal slaughter within the campus.
Although the administration subsequently softened its position, students led by the Jagannath University Central Student’s Union slaughtered a cow on October 16 and organised a beef feast. The student’s union is run by Jamaat-e-Islami Bangladesh’s student wing Islami Chatra Shibir backed candidates.
On October 17, Bangladesh Khelafat Chatra Majlish held a similar feast, slaughtering a second cow and organising a Qawwali programme.
It is also important to note that Diwali celebrations and Kali Puja were organized on the Jagannath University campus this year. A pandal was set up for Kali Puja and students were seen creating ‘alpona’, a traditional Bengali art form drawn on floors, which is considered auspicious.
To sum up, a video related to the controversial beef festival on Dhaka’s Jagannath University campus in October is viral with the false claim that Jamaat student leaders objected to Diwali celebrations at the university. The statements made in the clip have got nothing to do with Diwali. Besides, Kali Puja was held on the campus like previous years.

'A lie' & 'nonsense' - Palmer committed to England, says Rogers
- Published
Morgan Rogers says any suggestion Cole Palmer is not committed to England "is a lie" and "nonsense".
Rogers scored the opener in Wednesday's 2-1 Uefa Nations League win over Croatia, with Harry Kane adding a penalty on his record-breaking 126th appearance for the men's side.
But his Chelsea team-mate, and childhood friend, Palmer had been left out of the squad after boss Thomas Tuchel said he "misses too many chances to impress".
The 24-year-old Palmer, who was also not called up for the World Cup, withdrew from the previous England camp in September citing a minor injury.
Forward Rogers, also 24, was asked about the criticism of Palmer following the win at Wembley, and told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He wants to be here.
"He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done.
"He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself.
"But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.
"It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie.
"You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it."
- Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel? 
  - Published6 days ago
- A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma 
  - Published5 November
Struggles under Tuchel
In the three years since his England debut, Palmer has only won 14 caps, scoring two goals - including one in the Euro 2024 final defeat by Spain - and having one assist.
That is despite scoring 50 Premier League goals with 24 assists.
He was named England's men's player of the year for the 2023-24 season after some impressive form, including his strike against Spain in the Berlin showpiece.
But Palmer has only featured in three of Tuchel's 27 games since he succeeded Gareth Southgate as manager.
Some sketchy form last season, though, meant the former Manchester City player missed out on the the summer World Cup, with England going on to finish third after losing to Argentina in the semi-final.
He was named in Tuchel's first squad after that, but withdrew despite having played in all Chelsea's league games to that point.
Tuchel said this week: "We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together.
"I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.
"We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."
But the German added: "It's not personal. We will never assume Cole is in the mindset never to come to the camp.
"Cole is always in our mindset but the competition is on."
Bellingham an example to follow
Palmer should not give up hope of getting back into Tuchel's good books.
Last October Jude Bellingham was left out of the squad for a friendly against Wales and a World Cup qualifier against Latvia.
The Real Madrid midfielder then ended up being a key part of the England team at the World Cup, scoring seven goals.
Former Three Lions goalkeeper Paul Robinson added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "You can see what Thomas Tuchel is doing when you look at what he's done with Jude Bellingham.
"It was only 12 months or so that Jude Bellingham was getting left out of an England squad. Jude Bellingham was getting left out of England starting XIs.
"Call it what you want, but it was management from Thomas Tuchel to make Jude Bellingham realise that he wasn't the lone star of this team. The team was the star. The team was better with Jude Bellingham in it, playing at his highest level.
"There was a lesson in his management skills with Jude Bellingham and I wouldn't be surprised if he's doing the same now."

Sheinbaum rebuts Trump, says no migrant caravans have reached US border since January 2025
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum says no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025
MEXICO CITY -- Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Thursday that no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, responding to his threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico stops migrants from traveling through its territory.
“Not a single migrant caravan has reached the north” since January 2025, Sheinbaum said at her daily news briefing.
Sheinbaum said a caravan of about 600 migrants traveling through the southern state of Chiapas had largely dispersed after its members were told that reaching the United States would be “very difficult.”
She said Mexican authorities were also in talks with another group of several hundred Honduran migrants, encouraging them to return to their home country.
Asked whether Mexico would use force to break up the caravans, Sheinbaum ruled out such measures, saying authorities have “extensive experience” accompanying migrants and explaining that they have little chance of crossing into the United States.
Trump’s latest tariff threat comes as Mexico and the United States continue negotiations aimed at reducing or eliminating duties Washington imposed on several Mexican products last year.
The talks coincide with a review of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, or USMCA, which began in July.
Mexico is seeking significant reductions in the 10% tariffs imposed on Mexican goods not covered by the trade agreement, as well as the 25% duty on medium- and heavy-duty trucks.
Negotiations have also addressed a 50% tariff on steel and aluminum and a 17% countervailing duty on Mexican tomatoes.

Indore (Madhya Pradesh): Ahead of singer Diljit Dosanjh's live concert scheduled for Nov 15 in Indore, a fresh series of bomb threat emails triggered a security alert on Thursday. The mayor's secretariat and three banks received threatening emails, with the secretariat being targeted for the third time.
Following the repeated threats, police intensified security checks and deployed bomb disposal squads to inspect the targeted premises.
Additional deputy commissioner of police (DCP), Crime, Rajesh Dandotiya said four threatening emails were sent on Thursday at 10.37 am, 10.53 am, 12.53 pm and 1.47 pm. The recipients included Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank, Bandhan Bank and the mayor's secretariat.
Police learnt about the emails by the afternoon and alerted teams in the respective police station areas. Security personnel first visited the banks to conduct inspections. Around 6 pm, a bomb disposal squad reached the mayor's secretariat and carried out a thorough search of the premises.
Bombs will explode at Diljit's show, don't send your children
The threatening emails specifically mentioned Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert, warning that bomb explosions would take place during the event and advising parents not to send their children there.
The warning has prompted police to remain vigilant ahead of the concert. However, investigators suspect the emails could be hoaxes intended to create panic. Police are examining the threats and attempting to identify those responsible.
Dewas resident's email account hacked
During the investigation, police came across the name of Nikhil Gupta, a resident of Dewas who works for a private company.
Dandotiya said investigators discovered that Gupta's email account had been hacked in March or April this year. Gupta had been attempting to recover access to the account for several months.
Police recorded his statement and examined the account's login history. Technical analysis revealed the use of two foreign Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and a virtual private network (VPN), including a suspicious US-based IP address.
The Crime Branch is continuing its investigation into the source of the threatening emails.

LastWave, Musify, Convx, Spotube, and SimpMusic are free open-source clients for YouTube Music and Spotify. They unlock premium perks without subscription fees or ad tracking, offering background playback, offline downloads, time-synced lyrics, lossless audio, and customized interfaces without locked controls.
Subscription prices are going through the roof. And when you stack multiple subscriptions together, it can put a big hole in your pocket. For listening to music, we usually depend on Spotify and YouTube Music. They are the default music streaming sources for millions across the globe. Though there are alternatives from which you can hear high-quality audio, they just can’t match the ease of popular apps. But you are bombarded with ads, and several features are locked behind a paywall unless you pay.
Thankfully, you don’t have to search the internet for free options. Developers around the world have built free apps that give you many of those perks. Below are five of the best, what each does well, and what to watch out for before installing.
Table of Contents
Why are open-source music apps worth a look?
To be clear, most of these apps are clients. This means that they don’t store any music themselves. They plug into a service like YouTube Music and show it in a cleaner, ad-free interface with extra features on top, which you’d usually get after paying for a premium subscription. For me, Spotify has been the go-to music streaming app, but slowly the app has become quite greedy.
After a few times, the next and previous song buttons get locked, and it asks you to pay to unlock them. I mean, what is wrong with companies today? Thankfully, I have now ditched Spotify and have picked one of the below open-source music options.
That has three practical effects:
- No ads and no subscription fees. Everything below is free.
- Most of these apps have no ad trackers or tracking SDKs.
- New features are constantly added, and some of them aren’t even available in paid apps.
The catch is that these apps rely on unofficial methods to fetch music, so they can break when YouTube or Spotify changes something. Treat them as great free alternatives, but not as rock-solid replacements. Let us take a look at the free alternatives.
Best free open-source music apps
LastWave
If you care about how your music sounds, LastWave is the one to install first. It’s a free YouTube Music client for Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. Most of us would care about the free music that we get with LastWave, but you will soon appreciate the quality of music that it offers. And since it is a YouTube Music client, you are getting access to almost every song that is available on YouTube.
The headline feature is lossless FLAC audio, up to 24-bit/192 kHz. When you press play, the song starts playing right away on the fastest available stream, and while you listen, the app fetches the lossless version in the background and switches over once it’s ready. On compatible phones and headphones, LastWave also plays the Dolby Atmos version of a song automatically. For those who own a USB DAC or a pair of IEMs, there’s a bit-perfect mode that sends raw, unprocessed audio straight to your device.
The app is packed with features that normally sit behind a subscription. The lyrics are synced word-by-word and pulled from sources like Apple Music, Musixmatch, and LRCLIB. There’s a 10-band equalizer with presets for thousands of headphone models, and smart playlists that build mixes from your listening history. Plus, you have the option to import playlists from Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube Music in seconds, and even sync your Spotify liked songs.
Musify
Not everyone wants a hundred settings and toggles. Some people just want to listen to their favorite music without having to deal with ads and a hundred pop-ups about purchasing the subscription between two songs. Musify is for people who just want to open an app, search for a song, and press play. It’s a lightweight Android app built around Material You, which means its colors automatically match your phone’s theme and wallpaper.
Using it is fairly easy. You search for songs, albums, artists, or playlists and start streaming over Wi-Fi or mobile data. If you want to save data or listen on a flight, you can download tracks and play them offline. It lets you create your own playlists, rename and reorder them, or import existing ones from online sources. The player shows lyrics so you can follow along. You can also control the quality of the audio.
There are no annoying banner ads, no audio ads, no sign-up, and no tracking inside the app, and the interface is translated into dozens of languages by the community. I found this to be a great choice for older phones, or for a parent or sibling who finds complicated apps annoying.
Convx
While most open source music apps work well, there are only a few that also feel nice to use. Convx comes in the second category. If you like iOS’s “Liquid Glass” design, then you would love Convx. It brings iPhone’s Liquid Glass design to Android, with frosted, see-through menus, floating controls, and album-inspired colors that change with whatever you are playing.
Under the pretty surface, Convx is a complete music player. You can browse and stream music, save songs for offline listening, build queues and playlists, set a sleep timer, change playback speed, and tweak the sound to your taste with an equalizer. What makes it stand out among the heavy hitters is its DJ-style playback. You also get automix, crossfade, and smooth transitions between one song and the next. Lyrics are synced word by word and come from several providers, plus it gets animated artwork.
Convx can play local files and even songs stored on a home server or NAS through SMB and WebDAV. You can choose the option to import your Spotify playlists, show what you’re playing on Discord, scrobble to Last.fm, recognize songs playing around you, and use Listen Together to sync playback with friends.
Spotube
Spotube is the veteran here, with over 46,000 stars on GitHub, and it works differently from the rest. Instead of being locked to one service like Spotify or YouTube, it runs on plugins. You choose your own music sources, metadata, and playlists through plugins made by the community, or if you’re good with it, you can write one yourself.
The biggest advantage is that it works everywhere. Spotube runs natively on Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. This means you can use the same app on your phone and your laptop. It’s small, fast, and light on data. You can import and sync playlists from popular music services or manage them locally. It gives time-synced lyrics from public lyric databases no matter which source you use. Offline downloads are supported, with proper metadata and ID.
Privacy is one of the biggest highlights of Spotube. It collects no telemetry and no user data. Installing it is also easy, because you can download it through winget, Scoop, Chocolatey, Homebrew, Flatpak, and F-Droid.
SimpMusic
SimpMusic is that one app that does everything. It’s a free YouTube Music client for Android and desktop that borrows many of Spotify’s best ideas. You can play music from YouTube Music or regular YouTube without ads, and it gets you background playback. You can browse the home feed, charts, podcasts and moods, search everything on YouTube, cache songs for offline playback and use Android Auto.
SimpMusic Wrapped gives you a year-in-music recap just like Spotify’s. Then there is monthly recap playlists and listening charts that stay on your device. There are three Now Playing styles, including one that looks like Apple Music, and the lyrics are synced in 12 languages. You can even share lyrics as an image.
You can switch to 1080p video with subtitles, skip sponsor segments with SponsorBlock, see dislike counts with Return YouTube Dislike, and use a 10-band equalizer with AutoEq headphone profiles.
Which one should you pick?
If you care most about sound quality, I would suggest LastWave. If you want something simple, pick Musify. If design matters to you, try Convx. If you want plugins and an app that runs on every device you own, choose Spotube. If you want the most features in one place, install SimpMusic. The best part is that all five are free and can be installed side by side, so you can try a few and keep your favorite. You will get access to unlimited songs from the best sources in good quality. Let us know which one you chose, and comment below if you have a different app that you use for listening to music.

Allow me to introduce you to the robot cat butler I’m developing with help from AI.
Using OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol, I taught a virtual version of Microduck—a cute robot from Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face—to walk around a room and identify any bengal cats in its vicinity. (The clip above shows the robot waddling toward a target feline; its eye view is shown top right.)
I’m still waiting patiently for a physical Microduck—please hurry up and ship it, guys—but simulated behavior is relatively simple, so it should transfer over to the real thing. I plan to have the robot automatically dispense a treat for my pet bengal, Leona, perhaps by bowing its head to release one from a 3D-printed, head-mounted storage chamber.
I was able to code and train the virtual robot in just a few hours, which is, quite frankly, incredible. Previously, this kind of thing might have taken me weeks to figure out. It was possible because OpenAI’s latest models are remarkably good at understanding and manipulating 3D representations of the physical world and then translating that into useful code, agentic actions, and robot training.
Real roboticists are using the latest models to do some amazing stuff. When OpenAI released Astra this past September, University of California, Berkeley professor Ken Goldberg and his students saw demos that showcased its ability to render 3D images. They wondered if it could help with the simulations required to train different kinds of robots. These simulations need to be incredibly detailed and extremely accurate to ensure that sophisticated behavior—a humanoid that can dance or a robot hand that can grasp—will transfer faithfully to the real world.
One member of Goldberg’s lab gave Astra access to an Nvidia tool called Newton, showed it a video clip of a real robot in action, and asked if it could create a simulation of the scene.
“What blew us all away was that within an hour it had produced a full 3D simulation with all the parameters set—the position of the camera, the lighting, the background, all the materials,” Goldberg tells me.
Astra is also able to automate much of the drudgery involved with training a robot in simulation, Goldberg says, by running experiments and examining the results.
This is precisely what I found while training the virtual Microduck. Along with GPT-6 Sol, I used an agentic harness from Nous Research called Hermes and a Nvidia DGX Spark, a personal computer that contains a powerful AI chip.
I’ve previously written about using agents and coding models to configure, program, and debug physical robots. Normally, this kind of work requires significant expertise; modern coding models make it a cinch. But OpenAI’s newest model went far beyond just writing code.
It used a piece of Nvidia software called Isaac Sim to feed instructions to a model that controlled the virtual robot, watch videos of it in action to assess how well things were working, and suggest tweaks to its training regime.
This process allowed me to train the Microduck to walk around without toppling over. I initially tried getting GPT-6 Sol to teach the robot to moonwalk—I fed it a GIF of Michael Jackson sliding across the stage, which it tried to copy—but after hours of effort, it only resulted in a very jaunty backward jog. (The robots don’t have us totally beat quite yet.)
Jim Fan, a researcher at Nvidia who has collaborated with Goldberg, says the way AI can now control robots mirrors how software agents function. LLMS can use models trained to control physical actions—visual language action (VLA) models—just as they access different software on a computer.
This week, Fan, Goldberg, and others open sourced an agentic framework for robots called Aspire, which allows a robot to discover and use new skills. One example: GPT-6 Astra figured out how to use a pair of robot arms to solve a Rubik’s cube.
“It picks it up, tries to twist it, but has the wrong angle,” Fan says. “Then it reasons for a very, very long time, but it eventually is able to solve it because it learns the skills over time.”
At the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL), held in Austin, Texas, this week, Fan gave a keynote speech in which he talked about the incredible realization that AI models can automate a lot of the work needed to have a robot do sophisticated things. Fan showed off a demo in which Astra was put in control of a robot arm and told to paint a picture of the Golden Gate Bridge. Using some paint and brushes nearby, it duly completed the task.
Of course, getting robots to work reliably and efficiently is still extremely difficult, requiring significant engineering expertise. The vision system on my robot duck does not work well enough to be deployed in a real product.
Still, the ease and speed of training robots with AI could soon have an enormous impact on manufacturing and e-commerce, and Goldberg says a number of industrial robotics and automation firms have shown an interest in the approach.
Much like vibe coding a few years ago, we may well see breakthroughs in “vibe robotics” as hobbyists and engineers realize how easy it is to program and train robots. And, assuming I can perfect my robot helper, Leona may never have to go without treats again.

There’s a specific mantra drilled into government workers, military officers, and intelligence personnel during counterintelligence briefings: “If she’s a 10 and you’re a 5, she’s a spy!” Or, as the US Army’s Counterintelligence Command posted on Valentine’s Day: “It doesn’t take a mathematician to figure out ‘10 + 5 = honeytrap.’” The very beautiful woman who is suddenly interested in your very ordinary existence probably has ulterior motives, is the message.
Jensen Huang surely doesn’t live a typical life—he’s a centibillionaire, the swashbuckling CEO of Nvidia, one of the hottest and most geopolitically consequential companies of the 21st century. Surely he’s aware of the possibility that he’d cross paths with intelligence assets. In fact, it’s hard to think of many companies in the world that would be a higher priority target for foreign intelligence agencies.
All of that makes the stock-shaking news this week all the more surprising. How did Huang get embroiled in a spy scandal that mixes infidelity, international espionage, the Trump administration, and the economic behemoth of the multitrillion-dollar AI industry?
The story kicked off just before Halloween, with a six-byline story in The New York Times reporting that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Starting somewhere between 2024 and 2025, Huang allegedly had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a one-time executive at a Singapore-based cloud provider known as Megaspeed. US intelligence agencies warned top US officials that they believed she was a Chinese intelligence asset. So far, Nvidia’s board, which has launched its own investigation, says it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that’s far from the only concern.
As one would expect, China has denied any nefarious plot centered on Jensen Huang. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson on Monday said, “The narrative about so-called Chinese spies is entirely based on groundless speculation—it’s nothing more than slander and smearing.”
But according to reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times, US intelligence officials also claim that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was reporting to China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. On Monday, Megaspeed said on LinkedIn that US authorities found “no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities." (There’s no indication so far that Alice Huang, a one-time Chinese state journalist, is an employee or “officer” of Chinese intelligence; she’s believed to be an “asset,” an outsider who aids an intelligence agency, sometimes for pay, sometimes not.)
China, though, has elevated economic espionage to a core pillar of its economic and military development, stealing the designs for everything from US fighter jets to solar panels and commercial paint recipes. “Honeypots” or “honey traps”—positioning an alluring operative to seduce or develop a relationship with a key target—are one of intelligence’s most infamous and well-established strategies. French officials have warned specifically about Chinese honeypots since at least 2011, when intelligence reports cited a pharmaceutical researcher who was seduced and then blackmailed by a Chinese spy operation.
Over the past quarter of a century, as Silicon Valley emerged as a center of political and economic power, it has become a key focus of Chinese intelligence. In one plot, a Chinese national named Fang Fang spent years trying to cozy up to Bay Area politicians, including then US Representative Eric Swalwell. (While intelligence officials at the time reportedly believed Fang to be an operative, law enforcement officials never brought any charges against her). When traveling to China, US business executives have become accustomed to leaving their regular phones and computers at home and using burner devices to prevent the installation of spyware or malware (as I did, when I traveled to China for WIRED in 2019 to report on Huawei). In 2012, when Leon Panetta was making his first trip to China as defense secretary, he and his team were advised to bathe and shower in the dark in the event his hotel room was bugged. Last year, the threat of honeypots prompted the US government to explicitly ban personnel working in China and Hong Kong from engaging in romantic or sexual relationships with Chinese citizens. More recently, US officials joined with allies to warn about China’s increasingly sophisticated “LinkedIn espionage”: using the business-focused social networking site to recruit and build relationships with unwitting executives.
Alice Huang’s Megaspeed, for its part, is a major Pacific region player in cloud services focused on the advanced computer chips that are the heart of Nvidia’s business. The Biden administration had sharply limited the export of cutting-edge chips globally to slow China’s development of AI, but Jensen Huang has successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen those restrictions.
Speaking at a press conference on Monday, Donald Trump denied having prior knowledge of Alice Huang’s potential espionage. “I didn’t hear about it then, but a lot of people have heard about it, and Jensen totally denies that,” Trump said. “I asked him that question: ‘Did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’” On Tuesday, the Times reported that Marco Rubio had briefed Trump in May, right before Jensen Huang joined the President on Air Force One for a trip to China.
The veracity of Trump's claims will surely be investigated, especially in the context of the famous Watergate maxim: “What did the president know and when did he know it?” Nvidia’s CEO has been publicly linked to the Megaspeed executive since at least 2024 and Alice’s husband, Kang Weigh, has reportedly known Jensen since the 2010s. WIRED’s Lauren Goode reported on Monday that Jensen Huang, starting in 2025, hired Risa Heller’s crisis communications firm, which is well-versed in handling public sex scandals. This spring, secretary of state Marco Rubio evidently helped craft a classified memo inside the administration warning officials about Jensen Huang’s potentially compromising relationship.
Jensen Huang—who has developed an important reputation as AI’s #1 cheerleader at the frontier of AI labs—is now stuck in an awkward situation. Is he an idiot, unaware that his paramour might have been a foreign intelligence asset? Merely reckless with his own reputation, fiduciary responsibility to Nvidia, and the technological security of the United States? Or a witting accomplice to undermining US national security?
Regardless of the truth, Nvidia loses. Shareholders have ridden a roller-coaster that has seen Nvidia’s stock rise by about 600 percent over the past five years, becoming the world’s second-most valuable company. In the past month, the stock has plummeted by a quarter. The disaster for Nvidia is just beginning, it seems, as lawsuits loom, including by its own shareholders.
Similarly, the Trump administration is likely to face real questions from the newly Democratic congress: When were the president and other top officials briefed about this intelligence threat? What communication, if any, did they make to Nvidia and to whom? Should more have been done by US intelligence to block Alice Huang from having access to Nvidia and its CEO?
The fact that Megaspeed is a major customer of Nvidia makes everything more complicated. Indeed, reports have circulated for at least a year that the US was concerned that Megaspeed was diverting chips to Chinese intelligence agencies, an allegation that could have massive consequences for the global AI race. Bloomberg this week reported that Megaspeed's subsidiaries have purchased billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and that an audit requested by the US government last year found that Megaspeed couldn’t initially account for some 50,000 chips it had purchased.
Meanwhile, Nvidia’s Huang and President Trump developed a uniquely close professional relationship. They’ve met multiple times as Huang has pushed to loosen Biden-era export controls, which Trump has repeatedly relaxed; Huang has donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project; while en route to Beijing earlier this year with a delegation of tech leaders, including Elon Musk and Tim Cook, Trump’s Air Force One actually made a special stop in Alaska to pick up Huang; Huang also attended a White House state dinner for Chinese president Xi Jinping and Trump, who in turn, awarded him a National Medal of Science earlier this fall.
The implication that Trump knew and did nothing for a year would make this one of the greatest counterintelligence failures of the past decade. There will be consequences: Across history, many have gone to prison for honeypot scandals; a former adviser was arrested just last year in a similar plot; though he was acquitted of committing economic espionage, he was convicted for making false statements to investigators.
Even in normal circumstances, corporate America’s tolerance of CEO misbehavior has shrunken dramatically. In recent years, CEOs at companies as varied as Nestlé, Kohl’s, BP, NBCUniversal, and the railroad Norfolk Southern have all resigned or been forced out after inappropriate relationships that violated company standards.
If Nvidia were any other company and Jensen Huang any other CEO, the facts of the scandal currently known would be enough to topple some heads. But Trump is still president, and November is only a third over. It’s not even clear that this will rank as the biggest scandal of the month—but it should.

Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
President Trump's efforts to remake Washington, D.C., have dominated his second term, even after his party's resounding midterm defeat.
He started his election week at the scandal-plagued Reflecting Pool and ended it with an order declaring his gilded Oval Office a national monument to "make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space."
That proclamation, like any executive order, could be undone by a future president. But many of Trump's construction projects are changing D.C. in more permanent ways.
His administration has already downed hundreds of trees at East Potomac Park and demolished the East Wing of the White House to make space for a ballroom — which he called "the safest place in Washington" as he showed it to reporters the day after the midterms.
Trump has taken a uniquely unilateral approach to construction, packing regulatory commissions with his allies and bypassing Congress entirely. Most of his projects — from the triumphal arch to the Kennedy Center — are now playing out in court.
Critics accuse the Trump administration of skirting federal laws and misleading judges in its effort to progress as quickly as possible before the end of his term.
Democrats have vowed to use their soon-to-be congressional majority to push back on what they describe as Trump's "vanity projects."
When asked about that, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told NPR in an email that "no other president has done more to beautify our Nation's interior than President Trump." He cited park cleanups, the Reflecting Pool and the White House helipad and ballroom as examples, and said Democrats "should work with President Trump to make our nation's capital beautiful again."
Rep. Jared Huffman, D.-Calif., told NPR in an interview that the Trump administration has "played this game of Catch Me If You Can, where they roll ahead with the bulldozers and the tree cutters … and they wait for courts to shut them down." He says a Democrat-led Congress will fight back.
"There's no way that we could look away while these sacred, iconic places are being permanently changed in ways that violate the law and could have really terrible lasting impacts," said Huffman, the top Democrat on the House Natural Resources Committee, which has a legislative purview over public lands and national parks.
Huffman says blocking Trump's construction projects — and holding people accountable for potential wrongdoing — will be a top priority when he leads the committee. Earlier this week, he sent letters ordering dozens of administration officials and private companies to preserve their records for a future investigation.
"Whether it is the arch or … or the East Potomac golf course or any number of other examples around the United States capital, that is federal land, and we have a direct statutory responsibility to either authorize those changes or to stop them if they're proceeding without the proper authorization," Huffman said.
What would that actually look like? Democrats have many tools at their disposal, from legislation to lawsuits. But experts say only two are likely to succeed: funding and oversight.
Democrats could block funding for specific projects, potentially as soon as next month
Congress could — at least in theory — pass laws to block specific projects from moving ahead. Some Democratic lawmakers have already introduced bills to protect the Kennedy Center from demolition and prohibit the construction of an arch at Memorial Circle.
But Trump has promised to "veto everything," and Democrats won't have a big enough majority to override him on their own.
"Legislation in principle is the cleanest way of doing it, but it's also not achievable," said David Super, who teaches administrative and constitutional law at Georgetown. "So what they're likely to do is cut off funds."
The Constitution says that the federal government may spend money only if is appropriated by Congress. But Trump has neither sought nor received congressional authorization for projects like the arch and the White House ballroom — he maintains he doesn't need it.
Rep. Chellie Pingree of Maine is one of many who disagree. She's the top Democrat on the House committee that oversees funding for the Interior Department.
"Certainly Congress should have been involved, because we have the power of the purse," Pingree told NPR. "That is our ultimate tool. And Republicans have refused to use that. But we can use that in very many ways to block him or to use it for leverage."
Pingree says a Democratic majority will be able to write appropriations bills with clear language from the outset about where money can and can't be spent — and potentially take the president to court if he doesn't follow it.
Super expects Congress would prevail in such a challenge, because it has clear-cut authority over federal funds.
For example, he noted that some of Trump's D.C.-area beautification projects have been funded at least in part by diverted national park entrance fees. Congress could "cap how much money can be used in the greater Washington area, and force the money to be used in the Everglades and Yosemite and Great Smoky Mountains," he said.
Congress will have to make some appropriations decisions in the coming weeks, since it needs to pass a short-term funding bill by Dec. 11 to avoid a government shutdown. Democrats could use that opportunity to try to limit funding for at least one of Trump's construction projects.
Huffman has proposed language that would prevent Trump from using federal funds for the East Potomac golf course renovations, limiting them instead to repairs of the park's crumbling seawall. Pingree said she will join him in fighting to negotiate that into next month's bill.
"Whether or not the president will sign that with that in there, I don't know yet," she said. "But certainly those are the most … immediate crisis points … People want the president to stop cutting down the trees on the golf course and stop trying to take that over, and they want to make sure that no shovel goes into the ground on building the arch."
Earlier this year Pingree introduced an amendment that would have outright blocked construction of the arch; it failed along party lines. She wonders whether any Republicans might vote differently after the midterms, given the message Americans sent at the polls.
"They want the president to be focused on the issues they're dealing with: the cost of health care, the cost of food, the cost of gasoline," she said. "And if every time the president gives a speech, he's either standing in front of the Reflecting Pool, which he spent millions of dollars on, or showing you the new marble choices he's putting into the ballroom, it just makes a lot of people mad."
Pingree said she's been surprised to hear how strongly people feel about these projects – even people well outside D.C. And she agrees with them that potential corruption and misuse of taxpayer dollars are worth fighting: "After the first of the year, we will use every tool in our toolbox."
Democrats want to hold people and companies accountable
Lawmakers and experts acknowledge that not every project is reversible, or potentially even worth the fight. Huffman suggested he will focus on bigger projects, and ones that are moving too fast for courts to adequately rein in.
"Are we going to throw all of our efforts at stopping the gilding of every statue in Washington, D.C.? Probably not," said Huffman. "But these are iconic places that we're talking about, with permanent damage that we need to engage on to try to prevent."
Even so, Democrats could decide that certain construction projects are "the price they pay for other priorities," said Claire Leavitt, a professor of government at Smith College. Voters made clear they want lawmakers to focus on ending the Iran war and making life more affordable, big asks that may take a lot of political capital.
"And that's not corruption or Democrats not doing their job," Leavitt said. "It's just the natural trade-offs of dealing with who you're dealing with, and understanding that what matters to Trump more than anything seems to be building the arch, building the ballroom … remaking the Kennedy Center."
Whether or not these projects move forward, Congress can provide a fuller public accounting of how they came to be — in the hopes of preventing more in the future.
"They can gavel in hearings. They have agenda-setting power," Leavitt said. "They determine what the public hearing roster is. They decide which witnesses to invite. And that means they have a unique opportunity to draw negative public attention to the Trump administration."
That may be easier said than done, especially with an administration that has pointedly refused to comply with congressional oversight and is now warning Democrats that their future investigations could constitute criminality. Huffman was coy when asked how he is preparing to handle such challenges.
"We are going to have to have a strategy and a plan to do these things that prior Congresses have never imagined they would have to do," he said.
One investigative priority, lawmakers say, will be following the money — especially when it comes to donations for the ballroom and other projects. Leavitt says that focus has an added benefit: Private companies and individuals are likely more willing to testify than a member of the administration.
Another example: Congress could subpoena for information about the decision-making processes of the Kennedy Center board and the physical state of the building, which trustees say must be closed for two years of repairs. And it can put that information in the Congressional — and therefore historical — Record.
"Both the current public can make its judgments, and history can make its judgments," Leavitt said.
Leavitt said oversight can often lead to policy change in the longer term. For example: The committee investigating the Jan. 6 insurrection didn't stop Trump from eventually pardoning Capitol rioters, but it did lead Congress to pass an electoral reform act.
"The frustrating part about congressional oversight is Congress can draw attention to a problem, and they can demand accountability for something that's already been done," Leavitt said. "But it's very hard for Congress to stop something from happening that the president is determined to do."
Super agrees that Democrats are playing a long game. He expects to see more bipartisan support after Trump leaves office for preventing future presidents from following his playbook.
"The process in the past has been built on trust, and President Trump certainly broke that trust in numerous ways," he said. "Laws can be written so that we don't depend on trust, we depend on law. And I'm guessing we're going to do that."

So, you think you’re an Elder Scrolls superfan? You say you’ve been there since The Elder Scrolls Arena on MS-DOS and have logged hundreds of hours in The Elder Scrolls Online? You say you’ve bought all of the roughly 5,000 re-releases and remasters of Skyrim that have been made available in the last 15 years?
Tell me, then: What do you think of The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey?
What’s that? You’ve never played Shadowkey? You weren’t there day one back in 2004, Nokia N-Gage in hand, ready to experience the game’s 176 x 208 resolution mobile hack-and-slash RPG combat for yourself? And you call yourself a real Elder Scrolls fan?
Well, don’t worry. Now you can fill in this crucial gap in your history without even having to track down functional, decades-old N-Gage hardware. That’s thanks to Shadowkey: Reforged, a free fan-made PC port that pairs updated art with the original game files and scripts for an upscaled, 4K experience that runs natively on PC, no N-Gage or emulator needed.
A few decades of upgrades
Moving from a pre-iPhone mobile game to a modern PC obviously comes with major graphical upgrades, powered by a completely rewritten PC graphics engine. What was once a cramped portrait orientation on the N-Gage has now been expanded for a 16:9 monitor standard that displays at up to 120 fps (though the game’s logic still matches the original game’s 25 fps). In addition to newly retextured character and environmental models, the new port also sports small touches like bloom lighting, rippling water, and an upgraded interface with sharper text rendering than was possible on an ancient mobile phone.

Britain’s Prince William will attend the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony in Mumbai on November 17, marking the first time the global environmental awards, which he founded in 2020, will be held in India. The sixth edition of the event is expected to bring together 5,000 guests, including environmental innovators, business leaders, philanthropists and celebrities from across the world.
The organisers announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that the awards ceremony will conclude a series of environmental initiatives and discussions scheduled from November 13 to 17 across Jaipur and Mumbai. The programme will focus on climate change, air quality, waste reduction, ocean conservation and nature restoration.
The ceremony will recognise 15 finalists across five categories — Protect and Restore Nature, Clean Our Air, Revive Our Oceans, Build a Waste-Free World and Fix Our Climate. Five winners will be announced during the awards night.
India has produced more Earthshot Prize finalists and winners than any other country, according to the organisers. This year’s Indian finalists include Mahila Housing Trust and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, while previous winners from the country include Boomitra, Kheyti, S4S Technologies and Takachar.
The awards ceremony will feature Indian and international personalities, including Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Shreya Ghoshal, Sonam Kapoor, Rami Malek and Simone Ashley. British band Take That will perform in India for the first time, alongside Indian composer Shashwat Sachdev. Mumbai-based all-female hip-hop collective Wild Wild Women and pianist Merlin D’Souza will also perform.
Jason Knauf, CEO of The Earthshot Prize, said the event would highlight environmental solutions and support innovators working to address global challenges.
“The Earthshot Prize is coming to India to celebrate global innovation, entrepreneurship, culture, young people and environmental leadership,” he said.
“We are spotlighting the people building a better future, backing them, and helping their ideas go further and faster,” he added.
As part of the programme, the Jaipur Momentum Retreat will be held from November 13 to 15, bringing together the 2026 finalists, partners and environmental leaders to discuss future climate action.
In Mumbai, the Generation Earthshot initiative, scheduled from November 14 to 17, will bring together 130 young climate leaders from India, Africa, Asia-Pacific and Latin America for leadership workshops and local engagement activities.
The Impact Assembly, scheduled for November 16, will bring together business leaders, philanthropists, innovators and government representatives. Organisers said new partnerships, investments and expansion initiatives involving partners such as IKEA, Amazon and Uber are expected to be announced to support environmental solutions developed by Earthshot finalists and winners.
The programme will also include the I CAN Earthshot Challenge, a competition for children aged nine to 17, organised in partnership with Alana and Design for Change. According to the organisers, the initiative has involved one million children from 15,000 schools across 24 Indian states.
Fifteen finalist teams will participate in a two-day programme in Mumbai, culminating in an awards ceremony at the Museum of Solutions on November 17. Five winners will each receive a cash prize of $2,000.
The main Earthshot Prize awards ceremony will begin at 7 p.m. on November 17, following a green carpet event at 5 p.m. A press conference featuring the winners is scheduled for 9.30 p.m.
The Serum Institute of India is sponsoring the summit, while Prime Video will serve as the exclusive global streaming partner for the awards ceremony. The ceremony will stream globally from November 30 in more than 240 countries and territories, in over 40 languages.
Founded by Prince William in 2020, The Earthshot Prize aims to identify and support environmental solutions, intending to recognise 50 winners over 10 years.

The Humble Bundle storefront for buying games and other software recently got a new look, but on the settings page, it no longer offers a way to add or update two-factor verification methods, as reported by Kotaku. PC Gamer also points out that there are Humble Bundle support pages discussing two-factor verification, and the writer for the publication said that they had set up two-factor verification on the old version of the site.
Humble Bundle redesign removes two-factor verification from settings
A new look for the Humble Bundle storefront is missing an important security feature that was previously there.
However, it does appear that, at least as of now, there is some form of two-factor verification. When I tried logging into my Humble Bundle account while writing this article, I was prompted to check my email for an access code before I could access my account. While logged in, I was able to update my password, but I didn’t have to enter my old password to be able to do so.
For what it’s worth, my passwords app also shows that I set up a rotating two-factor code for Humble Bundle at some point. I was not asked to input that at any part of my login process today.
Humble Bundle owner IGN Entertainment and IGN parent company Ziff Davis didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

Quick Answer
Nothing OS 5 brings a bunch of useful upgrades, from on-phone widget creation and new lockscreen clocks to split Quick Settings, Dual-View Video, easier iPhone sharing, the Glyph app, translucent themes, smarter QR scanning, and the new Geist font.
Nothing has updated all of its eligible devices to the latest version of its operating system, Nothing OS 5. It runs on top of Android 17, and in typical Nothing tradition, is clean and uncluttered. And while it might seem broadly similar to its predecessor, there are a number of interesting new features – some important, some seemingly trivial – beneath that familiar surface. So if you have a Nothing phone and it has received the Nothing OS 5 update (there is a list of supported devices with rollout timelines here: https://in.nothing.tech/nothing-os), here are eleven things you must try out.
Table of Contents
Appy fizz: Now build snazzy widgets right on your phone, no coding experience required
One of the biggest innovations of the Nothing ecosystem was the introduction of Essential apps that let users, even with no coding knowledge, make widgets. In the past, you had to access Essential Apps on a computer to be able to make these widgets. Now you can do so right on your phone. And it is as easy as easy peasy apple squeezie. Mind you, you still need to sign up for Essential Apps and be part of a waiting list before you can get into design mode. No download is needed – the Essential Apps app comes to your Nothing phone when you update the phone to Nothing OS 5.g
Get a gooey or an info-loaded lockscreen clock!
On to the really serious stuff now. Perhaps the most noticeable visual change in NothingOS is the addition of two lockscreen clock widgets – Gooey and Micrographics. The Gooey clock has a bold and fluid look, with numbers looking a little melted. It is very eye-catching and, well, different. Those who want a truckload of information on their lockscreen and who opt for Micrographics get details like day, date, weather, temperature, upcoming appointments, and, of course, the time, all in rows that give it a very business ticker feel. This is how you clock into this feature:
- Long-press on the lock screen of your phone. This will show a Customize lock screen text bubble. Tap on it, and then tap on the fingerprint scanner to get into the Lock screen edit zone.
- Tap the clock widget space, which shows the time, and you will see Clock face options.
- Gooey is the second option, and right next to it is Micrographics. Choose the one you want, and also tweak its color as per your wish.
- Tap on Done, and hey, it’s, well…done.
Our own preference is the Micrographics widget, which is incredibly handy. We hope they add email and other notifications to it as well.
Split those notifications and quick settings
In the past – as on many phones – swiping down on a Nothing phone showed one new notifications, and swiping further down gave one access to Quick Settings (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Brightness, Torch, et al.). Well, you can split them into two separate zones if you wish. Once done, swiping from one side of the top will give you access to Quick Settings, while swiping from the other will show notifications. To do this segregation, just follow these steps:
- Open Settings and go to Notifications
- Go to the Notifications and Quick Settings Option
- You will see two options: Separate and Combined (classic).
- Select Separate, and now Notifications and Quick Settings will occupy different parts of the top panel.
Find out how long you have been away from your phone
One of the coolest new widgets on Nothing OS 5 is the Away Time widget, which lets you know how long you have kept away from your phone, and shows it in a simple, clean widget that can be placed on your home screen or your lock screen. It is a nice way to know about the “me time” you have given yourself away from your phone. Getting it is as easy as pressing on any place on the lock screen or Home Screen, and then selecting the Away Time widget option. We suggest going for the larger (4 x 2) one because it just looks so much better, especially with that zen-like blue background.
Keep what matters on the Home Screen – use Collector
Another widget (yes, Nothing seems to really like them widgets) that is very handy is Collector. You just open it and place images of what you want to keep seeing or consider important in it, and it automatically cuts out what it sees as important and keeps it handy on the home screen. It has a wonderful fridge sticker vibe, and keeps what matters close at hand. Just long-press on the home screen and select it from the widget collection!
Glyph Interface? There’s an app for that – finally!
The Glyph Interface has been one of the most eye-catching features of Nothing’s phones. This is basically a collection of LEDs on the back of the phones that light up in different patterns, showing notifications and battery levels, letting you know who is calling, controlling volume, setting timers, and doing more, all on the back of the phone. There was a catch, though. The Glyph UI had to be controlled from the settings of the phone, which seemed to be a rather roundabout way of doing things. This has now been fixed with the Glyph app, which gives one direct access to the Glyph Interface, letting one tweak it without having to get into the Settings. No downloads needed – the Glyph app appears on your Nothing phone the moment you update it to Nothing OS 5.
Lights, camera action…with both front and back cameras
Nothing OS 5 gives you the option to shoot videos using the rear as well as the front camera simultaneously. One can choose from having the footage one below the other, or having the selfie camera in an inset and the main camera in the larger part of the display. To access the option:
- Launch the Camera app
- Scroll across to More and choose Dual-View Video
It would have been nice to be able to take some stills with this feature, but as of now, it is limited to video.
There’s a glassy, classy “translucent” theme
Yep, your Nothing phone is now on the glass UI bandwagon. Mind you, this option is not turned on by default. You will need to follow these steps:
- Go to Settings, and then choose Customization
- Choose Theme & Style, and then choose Translucent. You can opt to have a dark theme in this if you wish.
- Honestly, it is not exactly eye-popping as of now. The translucence seems mainly to be around the widgets, and the app icons are not translucent. But it is a good starting point.
Scan that QR code, even if it wobbles
This is a pretty minor and yet handy change in Nothing OS 5. While camera icons have all been polished, a tiny yet useful tweak is in scanning QR codes, especially when using the scanner in crowded places or in slightly wobbly situations (think of paying in a moving vehicle). Now, when you use the camera to scan a QR code, the link it leads to remains on the screen, even if your hand moves and the QR code goes off or the code itself wobbles a little. So scanning codes is a whole lot easier, and you don’t have to bother about lining up the camera with the QR code all the time.
Send images to THAT friend with the iPhone easily (no app needed)
With Nothing OS 5, sending images to iPhones is pretty easy. Here’s how you do it:
- Ask your friend to switch on AirDrop on their iPhone and allow everyone to send images to it.
- Select the images you want to send on your Nothing phone.
- Select the Quick Share option, and then select the Use QR Code option.
- Scan the QR code with the iPhone’s camera. The images will be transferred.
Get the new font, Geist
Nothing’s marketing communications look very distinct because they use a font called Geist. Well, with NothingOS 5, you can now use Geist as the default font on their Nothing phones. This is how one does it:
- Head off to Settings again, and this time go to Display.
- Choose Font & Display Size.
- Once there, you can choose Geist as your default font.
- Once again, the difference is not going to jump out at you, but will become apparent as you use the phone.

Jensen Huang has reportedly resigned as the chief executive officer (CEO) of chipmaker NVIDIA. This brings the curtains down on Huang’s 33-year old tenure as the head of NVIDIA, the company he cofounded in 1993.
According to Reuters, the company’s board said that Huang had stepped down as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect.
This follows revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, one of which involved a woman accused of spying for China.
Meanwhile, chief financial officer (CFO) Colette Kress will take over as the interim CEO of the company. She will retain her role as the head of finance. The board will now reportedly consider both internal and external candidates to appoint a new successor to Huang.
