On the intervening night of November 8 and 9, over 250 PM2.5 data points from Delhi were missing on the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) website, according to an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).
Scientist and air quality analyst Manoj Kumar tweeted the statistics in the early hours of November 9. According to him, out of the 59 monitoring stations, as seen on the official website of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation.
Missing hourly PM2.5 data raises concerns over Delhi’s air quality assessment.
Since midnight on 8 November until 5 am on 9 November, 227 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation.
A key concern is that many missing readings occurred when concentrations approached the monitoring instruments’ upper measurement limit of 1,000 µg/m³. These observations should not simply be treated as missing when calculating hourly or daily averages or deriving AQI. Doing so could underestimate pollution levels. For a conservative assessment, such readings should be flagged as potentially exceeding the measurement range, with 1,000 µg/m³ considered as a lower-bound value rather than treating them as zero or excluding them without qualification.
Mundka recorded the highest number of missing hourly observations (10), followed by Dwarka Sector 8, IIT Delhi, Nehru Nagar, Pusa IITM and Uttam Nagar, with eight missing hours each.
There is also an unusual pattern at some stations. IGNOU Maidan Garhi, Cantonment Area, Siri Fort and Tikri Kalan recorded PM2.5 concentrations below 30 µg/m³ (Cleanest) during parts of this episode. Given the pollution levels elsewhere, these readings warrant verification for possible instrument or data-quality issues before being used in final averages or AQI calculations.
Reliable air-quality assessment during pollution episodes requires both complete data and transparent treatment of readings that exceed instrument measurement limits.
— Dr. Manoj Kumar (@manoj_kumar_nr) November 9, 2026
Air Quality Index, or AQI, turns air quality data for eight pollutants into one number and one name, providing an easy-to-understand picture of air quality. According to the All India AQI Dashboard, the pollutants are PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, Pb, and NH3. (Lead is not monitored at every station.)
Delhi’s average AQI on the night of Diwali was as follows, according to the CPCB.
However, between 1 am and 3 am on the Diwali night, over 30 monitoring stations were not showing any PM2.5 data. Over the course of the night, more stations failed.
A day after, as the mystery of missing data caused an outrage, the hourly air quality readings missing from the CPCB website became available on the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) website, which showed that the PM2.5 concentration went up to a staggering 3500 micrograms per cubic metre and beyond, which is around 60 times its standard value.
Below is the reading from Mundka station:
Below is the reading from JNU station:
Why does the Missing Data Matter?
India’s air quality figures come from monitoring stations run by state pollution control boards and committees, such as DPCC in Delhi. Stations send their readings to CPCB every 15 minutes. CPCB calculates each station’s AQI by finding a sub-index for every pollutant and taking the highest one. It then publishes the results on its portal, the SAMEER app and its daily bulletin.
A sub-index is the AQI score for a single pollutant on its own. Each pollutant is measured in different units and has a different “safe” range. For example, PM2.5 is in micrograms per cubic metre, and CO is in milligrams per cubic metre. So CPCB converts each pollutant’s reading to the same 0-500 scale, and that converted number is its sub-index.
If the PM2.5 has a sub-index of 75, SO2 has 63, and NO2 has 38, the station’s overall AQI is the highest of these, so here it is 75, driven by PM2.5. One bad pollutant is enough to push the AQI into a worse category, even if the others are fine.
If one looks carefully at the above screenshot from 12 midnight on November 9 from the Anand Vihar monitoring station, one would see that the 24-hour average of the PM2.5 pollutant is the 24-hour average AQI for that particular monitoring station. One would also note that the highest average sub-index determines the AQI.
Now, if PM2.5, which gives a measure of fine particulate matter in the air and is also highest during Diwali due to the bursting of firecrackers, goes missing, the average AQI reading underestimates the pollution in the air to a great extent. According to a Hindustan Times report, if one considers the released readings, Delhi’s AQI for 24 hours until 9 am on November 9 was 384 on a 500 scale against the 370 figure published by CPCB.
Why did the Data Go Missing?
According to Kumar’s post on X (shared when the missing data had not been released), Mundka recorded the highest number of missing hourly observations (10), followed by Dwarka Sector 8, IIT Delhi, Nehru Nagar, Pusa IITM and Uttam Nagar, with eight missing hours each.
Interestingly, the highest reading also came from Mundka at 3,744 µg/m³ at 2 am on November 9. JNU was at 3,023 at 4 am the same night and NSUT’s West Campus at 3,008 at 5 am. Eleven of DPCC’s stations went past 2,000 micrograms per cubic metre.
The CPCB released an official statement on November 10 addressing the data gaps, saying that particulate analysers like PM2.5 were calibrated for 0-1,000 µg/m³. Under the automated validation, hourly readings beyond that range are treated as “outside range” and left out of the computation. CPCB conceded this “may appear as a data gap” during extreme episodes like Diwali firecracker bursting. Those hours don’t count towards the 24-hour average for that station. It also stated that the methodology for processing data beyond the system’s design range is “under review”, with internal deliberations underway.
On November 11, Kumar posted on X, if the 255 missing PM2.5 data points were replaced with 1,000 µg/m³, the upper measurement limit cited by CPCB, the average showed a 49% increase, from 269 to 400 µg/m³.
Alt News spoke to Kumar, who also told us that while the DPCC continued to record data above 1000 micrograms per cubic metre, it was the CPCB, the body ultimately entrusted with calculating and releasing AQI findings, that did not register it. “DPCC had measured and displayed PM 2.5 concentration above 1000 on that day. But it was not reflected on the CPCB website.”
Explaining the process and the gaps, Kumar said, “Let’s say that the instrument’s operating range is between 0 and 1000. But if it is going above 1000, there will be some uncertainty, but uncertainty can be estimated.”
Even in his November 9 post, Kumar made the point that the readings had gone missing as the concentration readings approached 1000. “These observations should not simply be treated as missing when calculating hourly or daily averages or deriving AQI. Doing so could underestimate pollution levels. For a conservative assessment, such readings should be flagged as potentially exceeding the measurement range, with 1,000 µg/m³ considered as a lower-bound value rather than treating them as zero or excluding them without qualification,” he wrote.
Furthermore, to calculate AQI, one would need to have at least 16 hours in a day, if not all 24 hours of data. So missing out on important data points during peak pollution periods underrepresents the AQI value.
It’s also worth noting that aur quality monitoring is not cheap: A 2018 Hindustan Times report put the cost of a conventional station at up to Rs 5 crore.

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.
Also read | What new rules mean for allied health
The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.
The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.
The NCAHP has invited public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026 framed under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021.
Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.
“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.
This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.
“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.
By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.
An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.
Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.
The key features of the proposed regulations include standardised criteria and procedures for provisional registration; online application, verification and issuance of registration certificates with unique identification numbers; provisions for validity, extension, termination and appeals relating to provisional registration; bridge courses for skill enhancement, competency assessments and qualifying exams; supervised clinical training and institutional requirements for professional skill development; and transition to regular registration in the appropriate Central or State Register.
The NCAHP has now invited comments from allied and healthcare professionals, professional associations, educational institutions, State Allied and Healthcare Councils, healthcare institutions, experts, and the general public by December 4, 2026.

A molecular signal in the blood helps identify microscopic changes that precede the development of ovarian cancer, researchers have found, in a potential diagnostic breakthrough for a disease often discovered after it has already spread.
For decades, efforts to detect ovarian cancer earlier have focused on finding smaller tumours, the researchers noted in their report published on Tuesday in Nature Medicine.
“We asked a fundamentally different question: What if we could identify the earliest molecular warning signs before invasive cancer even develops?” study leader Rajan Gogna of the Hoag Family Cancer Institute in Newport Beach, California, said in a statement. Ovarian cancer often begins with microscopic changes in the lining of the fallopian tubes.
The precancerous lesions are known as serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC). The new study found that women with this precursor condition have elevated blood levels of an RNA molecule called Tu-Stroma.
When researchers measured Tu-Stroma in blood, they detected STIC in 92.3% of affected women and correctly identified 98.2% of healthy women. In women with genetic risk factors for ovarian cancer, approximately 72% of positive results would be accurate, while negative results would be correct nearly 100% of the time, they reported. “For women at high risk, this could transform how we approach prevention,” co-author Esha Madan, also of Hoag, said in a statement.
Many such women face difficult decisions about preventive surgery to remove their fallopian tubes and ovaries. “Today, decisions about preventive surgery are largely guided by inherited risk, without knowing whether precancerous lesions are actually present,” Madan said. “Our discovery could eventually provide that missing biological information.”

Five people were shot in Washington DC's Logan Circle neighbourhood, about a mile from the White House, on Thursday morning, with at least one dead, according to a witness cited by the Associated Press (AP).
Metropolitan Police Department interim chief Jeffrey Carroll said one victim died in the shooting. He added that the suspect shot himself while barricaded inside an apartment. According to Carroll, the suspect apparently had a dispute with the building's homeowners association.
The shootings were reported in Logan Circle, around a mile north of the White House. Police urged people to avoid the 1500 block of 15th Street, which includes a VIDA Fitness centre, St Luke's Episcopal Church and residential buildings, and is located near a Whole Foods supermarket. A large section of the block was cordoned off, while nearby schools were placed under lockdown.
According to AP, police had not immediately disclosed the identities or conditions of the five victims, the precise locations where they were shot or what led to the violence.
A witness, Ryan Dubicki, who was inside his nearby apartment around 8 am, said he heard approximately five loud bangs. He initially mistook the sounds for construction work because they were spread out, but later looked outside to find police officers across the area.
Dubicki said his apartment building's management subsequently sent residents a notice warning of a possible active shooter.
The shooting was reported near the intersection of 15th and P streets NW. The Washington Post reported that police were searching for a suspect and that MPD spokesperson Officr Lee Lepe described the incident as an active shooter situation. Lepe said police did not yet have a description of the suspect.
The police response involved several emergency teams, with nearby streets closed and residents and visitors asked to stay away. The federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) also sent agents to assist local authorities, AP reported.

The people of Iraq are in urgent need of better health care and their situation is deteriorating by the day. The UN has today appealed for at least $325 million in emergency funds to meet the immediate health, nutrition, water and sanitation needs of the most vulnerable populations. Out of this amount, the World Health Organization urgently appeals for $185 million.
This request is part of the wider United Nations humanitarian appeal for $2.1 billion to provide assistance to the people of Iraq over the next six months. This appeal is being launched jointly by all the UN humanitarian agencies in New York and Geneva.
WHO is already working in Iraq to provide badly needed medical assistance. The health status of the Iraqi people has been seriously affected by more than two decades of war and economic sanctions. Child death rates today are more than twice as high as they were in 1990: one in eight children dies before the age of five, one in three children is malnourished and one in four begins life as an underweight baby.
"Overall, the health of people in Iraq is poor and likely to get worse," said Dr Gro Harlem Brundtland, Director General of the World Health Organization. "This appeal is not an optional extra. It is the only way of stabilising the situation, and indeed improving it."
The three biggest child killers in Iraq are acute respiratory infection, diarrhoeal diseases and measles. Almost half of the country's 24.5 million people are children whose future depends on a massive and rapid improvement in the country's health and infrastructure.
Conflict is already adding to the strains on the health of the population and on the infrastructure on which they depend. For example, damage to the electricity and water supply in the southern city of Basra is expected to lead to additional health problems, particularly for children and other vulnerable groups. People elsewhere may soon face similar or worse emergencies.
A substantial investment is needed to provide essential care to people who are either injured in the conflict or whose health suffers as a result of damage to the infrastructure. In the months to come, more will be needed to begin rebuilding the most critical and most badly effected parts of the public health system.
That means building up the capacities of hospitals and health centres; it means providing some $60 million of medicines, medical supplies and equipment; it means repairing and rehabilitating vital hospitals and health centres.
There must be substantial investment in the ability to detect and respond to outbreaks of disease, in the training and equipment of health workers and in the health information which is vital to prioritise health work.
WHO today has more than 300 staff working hard in Iraq to support the health system and to bring badly needed medical assistance to people across the country. During the current conflict, WHO has successfully sent teams to help with an outbreak of diarrhoeal disease in northern Iraq and to assess the health needs of people who have left their homes. WHO is ready to do much more work across the whole country in support of the health system.
In the weeks and months to come, Iraq's health system will almost inevitably come under unprecedented pressure. Health is a crucial part of the economic and social system.

Starting Thursday, Whoop members can share their data from its wearables on the app’s new Whoop Humans social network. Users can make their metrics, activities, and achievements visible to other Whoop wearers, post Story-like “Moments” with photos and captions, and add comments and reactions on other members’ posts.
Whoop launched a social network where every user has a ‘verified heartbeat’
Whoop’s new Humans platform is like Instagram Stories with updates from your friends’ fitness tracker data.
Whoop claims its platform is “entirely human,” unlike other social media platforms that are “saturated with artificial intelligence, automated accounts and bots, and manufactured content.”
Whoop CEO Will Ahmed says Humans is “the most verifiably human network ever launched. Every account represents a real person with a verified heartbeat.” Whoop says its existing Teams social feature “will remain available,” allowing people to share strain, recovery, and sleep data along with group leaderboards.
In the Community tab in Whoop’s app, users can scroll through Moments from people they’re following, like tapping through your Stories feed on Instagram but with your friends’ fitness tracker data. In one of Whoop’s examples, swiping up on a user’s Moments post with a photo from their run shows a map with their route and details like their pace and distance. The Community tab also shows cards for people in your “community” with their sleep, recovery, and strain scores.
Whoop says users choose which activities, achievements, and metrics they want to share on Humans, including Recovery, Strain, Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate. Any activities marked as sensitive aren’t shared by default. There’s also an option to keep Moments posts private and a “Stealth Mode” for temporarily hiding health and performance data without changing your sharing settings.

In 1924, Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for his discovery of the mechanism of the electrocardiogram (ECG)”.
His work made it possible to record the electrical activity of the heart with greater accuracy. By developing the string galvanometer and establishing a standard method for interpreting its recordings, Einthoven helped turn electrocardiography into an important tool for studying heart function. Today, the ECG is routinely used to investigate irregular heart rhythms, detect signs of reduced blood supply to the heart muscle and identify evidence of previous heart attacks.

London court finds 2 Iranian men guilty of spying for Tehran
Two Iranian men have been found guilty of spying on journalists in London for Tehran
LONDON -- Two Iranian men who spied on journalists working for a Persian-language broadcaster in London were found guilty Thursday of spying for Tehran.
Jurors at Woolwich Crown Court in south London found Mostafa Sepahvand, 41 and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, to be working on behalf of the Iranian state and convicted of assisting a foreign intelligence service.
A third defendant, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was acquitted of all offenses against him.
“This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime,” said Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service’s special crime and counter-terrorism division.
He said the pair were promised rewards to send intelligence back to Iran, while Sepahvand was willing to go beyond surveillance to commit serious violence against their targets.
These included journalists for Iran International, Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, and a founder member of UK Lawyers for Israel, Jonathan Turner. Iran International is banned by the government in Tehran.
The defendants were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online.
“Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place,” Ferguson said.

Famed ship SS United States to be sunk off coast of Florida
- Published
A ship that was once the fastest in the world and is longer than the Titanic will be sunk off the coast of Florida and turned into the world's largest artificial ocean reef.
The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will soon become a home for sealife and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts.
Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner - which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times - to be preserved as a museum.
Instead, after being purchased by a Florida county, it will be added to the dozens of artificial reefs off the coast, as a land-based museum detailing the ship's history is also planned.
Before its retirement, the SS United States was known for carrying royalty and celebrities from the US the Europe, beginning in 1952 and ending in 1969.
A young Bill Clinton, before he was president, used the ship to cross the Atlantic. Former presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John Kennedy also travelled on the vessel.
The ship was moved from Philadelphia to Alabama last year for cleaning and remediation work. On Monday, it took its final journey from Alabama to the coast of Destin, Florida, where it will be sunk on Wednesday in a precision operation without explosives.
Stars including Marlon Brando, Coco Chanel, Duke Ellington, Salvador Dali, Walt Disney, Judy Garland and Cary Grant also boarded the ship during its sailing lifetime.
Before its purchase by the municipal Florida government, a number of proposals that would have seen the ship live a second life as a museum or a floating hotel failed.
Instead, the famed ship sat at various docks with various owners as legal battles played out.
The SS United States Conservancy group repeatedly attempted to keep the ship above water, but was unsuccessful.
Conservancy President Susan Gibbs - whose grandfather helped design the SS United States - said she was glad that the story of the ship would live on.
"[The ship] has always been this unabashedly American symbol that brings so many people together," Gibbs told CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

A claim is spreading online that Jan. 6 Capitol rioter Jake Lang, who was pardoned by U.S. President Donald Trump, crashed a cat convention in Seattle because he appeared to believe the event was for furries — people who identify with or enjoy dressing as anthropomorphic animals or creatures.
Videos of the alleged event and jokes about Lang's apparent mistake spread on X, Facebook and Threads. (Warning: Lang uses profane language and homophobic slurs in the video below).
Lang did, in fact, post videos of himself at Sea-Meow, a Seattle cat convention, with captions that claimed he "BUSTED UP" a "furry convention." Of course, it's impossible to know whether Lang actually believed Sea-Meow was a furry convention, or if he simply said that it was. 
Either way, however, it is accurate to say that Lang crashed a cat convention while publicly claiming that it was for furries. As such, we have rated this claim as true.
The video shows Lang yelling slurs at people wearing pink shirts and cat ears who appeared to be convention staff. Lang accused them of "sexualizing children" and spreading "homosexual and transsexual ideas." Lang also claimed the organizers were "mislabeling" the convention before one of the people in pink shirts stepped in.
"This is a convention for cats," the person tells Lang in the video. Lang, in response, doubles down, asking why there were furries at Sea-Meow. (Being a furry is not inherently sexual, and academic research indicates that furries are more likely to identify as such for nonsexual reasons, like social belonging.)
The "Sea-Meow" sign is clearly visible in Lang's videos, and there is no evidence the videos were generated using artificial intelligence.
While at least one person in a fur suit — the costumes furries are known for — was visible in Lang's video, Sea-Meow is clearly about cats, not furries. The convention describes itself as "the premier cat convention of the Purrcific NW, the mecca of cat people." Sea-Meow's stated mission makes it clear that it's focused on supporting cats, not furries:
Our mission is rooted in the celebration of our love of cats by bringing together all the cat people under one roof and supporting feline organizations around the United States in meaningful ways. We aim to connect our community, educate and spread feline awareness, inspire people to participate in the animal welfare community, and help cats conquer the world, one home at a time!
Programming for Sea-Meow, which ran Nov. 7 and 8, included panels with cat rescuers and a presentation by Jackson Galaxy, a cat behaviorist and YouTuber perhaps best known for hosting the now-defunct Animal Planet show "My Cat From Hell." Sea-Meow's website also said that 15% of ticket proceeds went to charities like the Seattle Animal Shelter and Feral Care, a nonprofit organization that provides food and shelter to "unadoptable cats."
Videos on Sea-Meow's social media largely show people of all ages cuddling cats, with nary a fur suit in sight. Sea-Meow's sponsors include Weruva, a cat food company, and BluePearl Pet Hospital, which operates specialty and emergency vet hospitals across the United States.
Sea-Meow's programming did include a "cat cosplay contest," but photos of example cosplays did not show any fur suits, instead depicting people dressed like Hello Kitty, a "taco cat" and other non-furry costumes.
We reached out to Sea-Meow to ask if the convention had any programming or policies about furries and if Lang ever actually made it past the doors, given that his videos are filmed outside of the actual convention building. We await a response.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has cautioned students and parents against enrolling in medical colleges without verifying their statutory recognition and regulatory approvals, warning that fraudulent institutions could be misleading aspirants through advertisements, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers.
In a recent advisory issued in compliance with directions from the Supreme Court, the NMC has urged students to independently verify a medical college’s approval status, permitted student intake, and admission permissions for the relevant academic year before seeking admission or making any payment.
The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida & Ors., an ongoing case in which the Court directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions. The directions came in the context of a reported instance of a purported fake medical college operating from a farmhouse and claiming to offer various courses.
The Commission has clarified that a medical college’s presence in an official list, or its previous operation, does not automatically establish that it has permission to admit students in subsequent academic years. Candidates must check the approval granted for the particular year and the number of seats sanctioned through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) records.
Verify with regulatory body
It has also cautioned students against relying exclusively on prospectuses, websites, advertisements, social media posts or documents such as purported Letters of Permission and approval certificates circulated by institutions or their representatives. Any doubts regarding the authenticity of such documents should be verified directly with the concerned regulatory authority.
For admissions governed by counselling procedures, candidates have been asked to use official channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), wherever applicable, or the competent State and Union Territory counselling authorities. The Commission has also advised students against making admission-related payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries.
Highlighting the importance of distinguishing between regulatory approvals, the NMC said affiliation, registration or recognition granted by one authority for a particular purpose should not be construed as permission from the Commission to conduct an MBBS course. Each statutory requirement must be independently satisfied.
Extraordinary claims
The advisory also asks students and parents to exercise caution when institutions make extraordinary claims about clinical training, hospital facilities and admission opportunities. The existence of a building, office or website, it said, does not establish that an institution is legally authorised to impart medical education.
Suspected fake medical colleges, unauthorised MBBS courses, forged permission letters and fraudulent admission offers can be reported to the NMC through its official communication channels. Complaints may also be made to the State or U.T. medical education departments, relevant regulatory authorities, and local police. Students have been advised to preserve advertisements, payment receipts, correspondence and website details as supporting evidence.
The Commission has separately clarified that courses in pharmacy, nursing, Ayurveda, and allied healthcare programmes fall under different statutory or competent regulatory authorities. Their recognition and approval must be checked with the respective regulators.
The advisory asks the public to refer to the NMC’s official website and relevant regulatory and counselling portals for updated information before proceeding with admissions or payments.

Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal.
Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.
Argentina has applied to the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos) for a ruling that would force Britain to suspend the drilling for oil in the North Basin of the Falkland Islands ahead of further arbitration.
The Sea Lion oilfield is about 130 miles north of the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory over which Argentina has a longstanding sovereignty claim.
Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, reportedly shared among his cabinet a photograph of the Argentinian legal team in Hamburg, describing it as “tremendous”, adding that “we are working on the Falklands issue like no one else in history”.
Addressing the tribunal on the second day of hearings, Kohen said that the dispute over the archipelago of 700 islands in the south Atlantic – known in Argentina as the Malvinas – did not mean that the area was a “legal black hole” and that the UK could do as it wished with its natural resources.
“The fact that the parties dispute sovereignty does not turn the areas surrounding the Malvinas into some kind of Dominium maris Britannici,” he said. “We are not in the 17th century … We are in an era where we should put an end to the last vestiges of colonialism.”
Ellie Reeves, the attorney general for England and Wales, told the tribunal’s panel of judges on Tuesday that Argentina was seeking to further its sovereignty ambitions by applying for suspension of the drilling.
She claimed that such a move would kill the Sea Lion project, with “disastrous consequences” for the Falkland Islanders and the companies involved. The UK claimed that the tribunal, which adjudicates over maritime matters, does not have jurisdiction to wade into matters of sovereignty.
Kohen, switching from French to English, said the UK had failed to mention in its submissions the “elephant in the room” or the “whale in the bathtub”. The UN regarded the Falkland Islands as a non-self-governing territory, he said, and had called in 1976 for both sides to refrain from taking decisions that would unilaterally change the situation before the sovereignty dispute was settled.
The exploitation of hydrocarbons would put the islands among the “highest ranks of wealth just below the principality of Monaco” while depriving Argentina of its rights to those resources, Kohen told the tribunal.
Argentina’s legal team claimed that suspension of the drilling, which is due to start in March next year and which could double the GDP of the islands, was urgent given the irreparable damage to Argentina’s rights.
The UK has claimed there is no urgency as oil extraction would not take place until 2028, before which an Itlos arbitration panel would have come to a conclusion on the future of the oilfield.
In his closing remarks to the panel of 20 judges, Mario Oyarzábal, a legal adviser to Argentina’s ministry of foreign affairs, said they rejected the UK’s attempt to characterise the proceedings as an attempt to litigate the sovereignty dispute.
He said: “The question before this tribunal is a much narrower one: whether, while the underlying dispute remains unresolved, the UK may unilaterally authorise or carry out new drilling for the exploitation of hydrocarbons in the disputed maritime area.”
Milei described the reclaiming of the Falklands as a “national cause” during his recent speech at the UN general assembly. Argentina invaded the islands in 1982 on the orders of the dictator Gen Leopoldo Galtieri. The 74-day conflict ended with the surrender of the Argentinian forces and cost the lives of 649 of its military personnel, 255 British military personnel and three Falkland Islanders.
The UK will offer further submissions on Wednesday.

Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
- Published
Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill.
Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.
Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future.
His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks.
Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.
On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.
Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear.
And US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, along with other Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, publicly demanded that Huang brief Congress on the matter.
If he refuses to appear voluntarily before any committee that calls him, he could be subpoenaed, one Senate staff member told the BBC.
Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.
According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.
Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.
Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.
It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.
Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.
Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.
Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.
The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.
Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming.
But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.
Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.
Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.
He is far from the first tech titan to become embroiled in revelations of infidelity.
Bill Gates of Microsoft and Jeff Bezos of Amazon had affairs exposed in the last decade. Both men are now divorced from their wives.
Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.
Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.
Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.
Because of Nvidia's size and success in recent years, such a drop can have a direct impact on the savings accounts of ordinary Americans.
Nvidia's value makes up about 7% of the S&P 500 index. That index is offered as a popular index fund in US retirement savings accounts.
Those account balances rise and fall with the changes of the stock market.

A team of scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) has identified critical weaknesses in the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis (TB), a finding that could pave the way for the development of new treatments against one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases.
The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025. Drug-resistant TB remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains.
Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB. The study sheds light on how the pathogen transports proteins within and outside its cells, a process essential for its growth, survival and ability to cause disease.
The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad.
Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network. These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.
“Protein secretion acts like a delivery system inside the bacterium and is vital for its survival,” said Dr Uppada. The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity. The results were striking: bacterial growth declined sharply both in laboratory cultures and inside immune cells, demonstrating that both pathways are essential for the pathogen’s survival.
Dr Priyadarshini Sanyal said further analysis revealed that disrupting these systems affected the export of more than 100 proteins in the SecA1 pathway and around 140 proteins linked to the Tat system. Researchers also observed structural damage to the bacterial cell membrane, making it unstable and more permeable. Proteins that normally remain inside the bacterium began leaking into the surrounding environment.
Dr Nandicoori said that these changes highlight the close connection between protein secretion and the maintenance of the bacterial cell envelope, a key factor behind TB’s persistence and resistance to treatment. The findings, published in the peer-reviewed journal Molecular & Cellular Proteomics, could help researchers identify new drug targets, although translating the discovery into effective medicines will require several more years of research.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded an Army soldier a medal on Thursday, one day after the soldier publicly reprimanded the Pentagon chief and his entourage for boisterous behavior near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery.
Spc. Thomas Iglesias received the Joint Service Commendation Medal for his conduct during Wednesday's Veterans Day observance.
"We love soldiers. We love standards." Hegseth wrote in an accompanying social media post. "Well done, Specialist."
These developments have spotlighted the specially selected soldiers from the Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, known as The Old Guard, who have guarded the nation's most sacred military memorial since 1948.
On Wednesday, Hegseth, his wife, and several senior aides were posing for photographs near the memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony attended by President Donald Trump. As the group departed, laughter from a member of Hegseth's party could be heard.
"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," Iglesias shouted, stopping his patrol to address the group.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell subsequently said the soldier had "correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum."
Who guards the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier?
The soldiers who guard the tomb, known as sentinels, are volunteers who undergo a demanding selection and training process to earn one of the Army's rarest military badges, the Tomb Guard Identification Badge. Business Insider previously documented the rigorous training and evaluations soldiers must complete to qualify for the role.
Over 735 soldiers have earned the badge since the Army started tracking sentinel numbers. Sentinels must be at least 5 feet 8 inches tall. Just eight women have held the job.
Sentinels are on duty at the memorial regardless of weather. Each follows a tightly choreographed ceremonial routine. According to Arlington National Cemetery, each sentinel marches 21 steps, pauses for 21 seconds, and repeats the sequence. The number symbolizes the 21-gun salute, the military's highest ceremonial honor.
The tomb contains the remains of unidentified American service members from World War I, World War II, and the Korean War.
The soldiers work on a three-team rotation schedule, working 24 hours at a time, and wearing wet gloves to improve the grip on their 1950s-era M14 rifle. Guards are swapped out every 30 minutes in the summer and each hour during winter. But when the cemetery is closed, postings last for two hours.
They are also responsible for preserving the dignity of the memorial and ensuring visitors observe its strict standards of respect. In a 2022 Army news release, one sentinel said it's normal to correct misbehaving visitors two or three times a day.
"It's usually just them being oblivious," the sentinel said. "They're talking and not realizing how loud they're being, or laughing or making jokes amongst their group. It detracts from the other people that are trying to pay their respect."

We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird’s blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers, and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy.
As previously reported, Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He’s been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year.
The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “Planet Claire” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn. Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a pun on “raygun,” of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird.

Supriya Sule rules out NCP merger talks, says ‘no one has approached me’
Her remarks came shortly after Maharashtra NCP president Sunil Tatkare said he saw no substance in the speculation surrounding merger talks.
Amid speculation over a possible reunification of the two NCP factions and a series of meetings between leaders from both sides, NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule on Thursday categorically ruled out any ongoing merger talks, saying the issue had ended for her with the death of then NCP president and Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar in a plane crash in Baramati on January 28.
Sule said she had neither received any merger proposal nor been approached by anyone on the matter.

Sule says Ajit Pawar's death changed everything
She acknowledged that discussions on reunification had taken place when Ajit Pawar was alive. Still, she said his sudden demise and subsequent developments had brought the matter to an end from her side.
Her remarks came shortly after Maharashtra NCP president Sunil Tatkare said he saw no substance in the speculation surrounding merger talks between the two factions.
Sule, who was in New Delhi, chose to break her silence on the speculation nearly two weeks after it gained momentum following a meeting between six senior NCP leaders and Union home minister Amit Shah on November 1.
The leaders were learnt to have indicated their support for a merger between the rival NCP factions, triggering fresh speculation about a possible reunification.
“I have not received any proposal for a merger, so I do not know which proposal you are referring to. No one has approached me or spoken to me about it,” Sule chose to begin with in response to questions related to ongoing merger talks.

'From my side, the matter ended'
When asked about several NCP leaders meeting NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar over the past week, Sule said she could speak only about her own experience.
“When my brother (Ajit Pawar) was alive, we held discussions about the merger of the two parties. He discussed the matter with all of us. A video of one such meeting, held at Govindbaug on January 17, is already in the public domain. The entire world knew what we were planning and the direction in which things were moving. However, my brother's sudden demise changed everything. From my side, the matter ended there.”
For the unversed, Ajit Pawar, nephew of Sharad Pawar, had split the NCP in July 2023 and subsequently secured the party's original name and election symbol after joining the ruling Mahayuti alliance in Maharashtra. Sharad Pawar was left leading the rival faction, which was allotted the name Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar). However, less than three years after the split, the two factions began exploring the possibility of reunification, with Ajit Pawar keen to bring the parties together by February 12. The process, however, was cut short by his death in a plane crash
She further refused to comment on the meeting between senior NCP leaders and the Union home minister, terming it an internal matter.
Tatkare was the first to publicly acknowledge on November 6 that merger discussions had taken place and that the two factions would have reunited on February 12 had Ajit Pawar been alive.
He was also part of the delegation that met Shah in New Delhi earlier this month, along with national working president Praful Patel and four other senior leaders. The meeting fuelled speculation about a possible merger. On Tuesday, Tatkare met Sunetra Pawar in Baramati, followed by a meeting with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis at his official residence, Varsha, on Wednesday.

FIFA has joined forces with the United Nations (UN) and the World Health Organization (WHO) in supporting the #BeActive campaign launched on the UN International Day of Sport for Development and Peace to encourage people to be #HealthyAtHome as the world comes together in the fight against COVID-19, today and every day.
WHO recommends all healthy adults do at least 30 minutes a day of physical activity and children at least 60 minutes per day. As part of this, #BeActive and remain #HealthyAtHome include the following suggestions along with any other form of recreation to stay healthy at home:
- Taking some online exercise classes,
- Dancing,
- Playing active video games,
- Jumping rope, and
- Practising muscle strength and balance training.
“We are delighted that football is strongly supporting the International Day of Sport for Development and Peace by asking everyone to #BeActive and to remain healthy at home during this difficult time,” said António Guterres Secretary-General of the United Nations. “FIFA has asked the football community, from member associations and clubs, to players and fans, to show their support, to put their rivalries aside and to show a new solidarity so we can overcome the coronavirus. This is an important lesson not only for today, but for every day.”
“More than ever, especially now, one thing must be clear to everyone, health comes first,” said FIFA President Gianni Infantino. “FIFA is delighted to support both the United Nations and the World Health Organization in amplifying the #BeActive campaign today, and we are encouraged that the football community is also playing an active role in ensuring the message understood globally. For the first time ever, we are all on the same team and together, with team spirit and positive energy, we will win.”
“WHO is proud to collaborate as part of the UN family with FIFA and football lovers worldwide to promote the importance of being active for both physical and mental health,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization. “The #BeActive campaign supports WHO’s drive to help people be healthy at home.”
The campaign kicks off with Real Madrid CF, FC Barcelona, Liverpool FC and Manchester United FC asking football fans to set aside their rivalries and to come together to #BeActive in order to defeat the coronavirus. Other clubs, including Club América, CD Guadalajara, Beijing Guoan FC, Shanghai Shenhua FC, Mohun Bagan AC, East Bengal FC, Melbourne City FC, Sydney FC, Auckland City FC, Team Wellington FC, CA River Plate, Olympique de Marseille, TP Mazembe, CR Flamengo and SE Palmeiras will also join the initiative in the coming days.
As part of the campaign, world-famous players share the following message: “At this time, even rivals need to stick together. We have to keep our distance, but we do not lose our focus. We can show solidarity by being active, and active means following the guidelines from the WHO.”
The video campaign will be published on various FIFA digital channels, with regular subsequent updates from clubs and players across the world during subsequent days. #BeActive is also being supported with graphics toolkits for the 211 FIFA member associations and various media agencies to facilitate additional localisation and to further amplify the message.
WHO, the UN’s specialized health agency, and FIFA, football’s world governing body, collaborate closely to promote healthy lifestyles through football globally and launched the “ Pass the message to kick out coronavirus” campaign last month to share advice effective measures to protect people from COVID-19.

Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
- Published
The tech world has spent the day digesting the extraordinary news that Jensen Huang - the charismatic, leather-jacket wearing chief executive of the multi-trillion dollar firm Nvidia - is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
None of us had that on our bingo cards for 2026.
Huang's alleged romantic affair with Alice Huang (no relation), the former CEO of a Singapore-based data centre company, has cast ripples far beyond his immediate family - undoubtedly on an emotional rollercoaster of their own - taking us to a crossroads at which technology, geopolitics and national security intersect.
In a nutshell, this is about the bitter rivalry between the US and China, as well as whether Jensen Huang has betrayed the US as well as his wife.
The US is locked in a fierce race with China to develop the best AI models.
"Whoever wins AI, wins," as US President Donald Trump puts it. He thinks that the country with the more dominant AI technology will benefit the most from it and, ultimately, will be the most powerful in the world. He may well be right.
Nvidia happens to make the best chips in the business for AI – so much so that it has been overwhelmed with demand.
It sets its prices accordingly: a single unit of the firm's latest kit for data centres starts at £37,000 ($50,000). A medium or large site might have hundreds of them.
The US administration initially slapped an export ban on Nvidia's more recent devices to prevent China from taking advantage of their superior capabilities. It has since softened the rules a little.
But there are suggestions that Alice Huang's company, Megaspeed, may have been involved in sneaking them into the country while she was in charge. Bloomberg reported that the firm bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia tech in November 2025. Megaspeed denies that it was used illegitimately.
For his part, Jensen Huang has lobbied heavily for the export rules between the two countries to be relaxed, arguing against the weight of general opinion that the AI race doesn't matter and that it would be no bad thing for China to become dependent on US tech.
"President Trump wants American to win and President Xi wants China to win, and it's possible for both of them to do so," he told the BBC last year.
I think it's safe to assume that neither country sees it that way.
- Could this be the end of 'Jensanity' 
  - Published1 day ago
The difficult questions Nvidia now has to try to answer include whether Alice gained special access to the firm's latest technology, either deliberately or not, via Jensen - and, if so, whether she shared it with Beijing or others.
We don't know when their affair began or ended, but there are numerous photos and videos of Jensen and Alice together at events. It is feasible that there were moments when they spent quite a lot of time together and Jensen has talked about always having an eye on his work.
China denies that she was engaged in espionage.
Interest in economic espionage is neither new nor unique to China. But many Western countries say that China does it on a grand scale, using a combination of technology tools and agents embedded in various organisations - including private companies.
China having access to significant enough numbers of Nvidia's chips to make use of them, or stripping them down and learning how to make its own versions, would infuriate the Trump administration, which is trying to keep its AI technology close to its chest.
Some models have even been withheld from the UK-based AI Safety Institute on the grounds that they are potentially too dangerous to be shared. The US does not want anyone having a headstart or misusing its innovations.
Another potential bombshell lies in the form of any national security information to which Jensen Huang may have been privy.
He is a man operating at the very top of the US elite - one of a handful of people who could probably walk into the White House unannounced and have tea with Trump. He has influence, he has access and he has powerful friends. It's quite possible that secrets were shared with him.
Nvidia says there's no evidence so far that he passed anything on and the firm has launched an internal investigation. Huang says he will co-operate and wants to keep his job - though if nothing else, he has broken Nvidia's own code of conduct, which states that company members should not have relationships with clients.
But can he survive?
At present, he has the backing of both the Nvidia board and Trump, who described him as "honourable" and speculated that there must have been a reason for what had transpired. In other words, he's not throwing his tech boss buddy under the bus.
Nvidia's share price has fallen but has not tanked spectacularly, suggesting shareholders are not abandoning the company under his stewardship in their droves either.
An AI industry with a weakened Nvidia would undoubtedly be a slower one.
And there isn't really a natural successor waiting in the wings to replace Jensen were he forced out.
Huang has run Nvidia for more than 30 years - to many, he is Nvidia. He has steered it through multiple crises and it was his decision for the firm to focus on AI before it was trendy.
He is known to be a demanding boss who expects staff to work long hours and to high standards. There are stories about him calling all-staff meetings to tell off individuals who had made mistakes. He has said this was to prevent others making the same errors – but you can only imagine how it felt for those on the receiving end.
While he awaits the conclusion of the investigation into his actions, Huang must hope that, despite not tolerating the mistakes of his colleagues in the past, they will be gracious about his own failings.
And he must also live with the irony that he was potentially caught out not by a sophisticated high-tech sting, but by the oldest trick in the book: a honey trap.

Producers Kelly McCormick and Allan Mandelbaum have revealed what drew them to How To Rob A Bank, saying the film’s unconventional script stayed on their minds for days after their first reading. Directed by David Leitch, the upcoming heist film combines high-octane action and humour with a story rooted in the viral world of social media.
How To Rob A Bank producers Kelly McCormick and Allan Mandelbaum reveal why David Leitch’s heist script stayed with them for a week
Recalling her first reaction to the script, McCormick said that its premise continued to occupy her thoughts even after she had finished reading it. “It was almost a week later, after we first read it, I said to David, I can’t stop thinking about that script. And he was like, you know, me either. There’s something about it, isn’t there?"
For McCormick and Leitch, the project also presented an opportunity to approach the heist genre differently while retaining the filmmaking sensibility associated with their production banner, 87North. She explained that the story's premise could connect with contemporary social conversations while delivering an entertaining cinematic experience.
“We were thinking about the sort of energy behind that frustration people are feeling,” McCormick said and went on to add, "Was there something to this script? And could we be part of that conversation in a way that felt very 87North, that felt very David Leitch-ian – that it could be fun and wild, but also put a message forward – be part of an important conversation our society is having right now, and strike a chord that so many people are feeling today?”
Mandelbaum also spoke about the creative partnership between Leitch and McCormick, and their ability to connect with mainstream audiences through their work at 87North. He said, “David and Kelly and what they’ve built at 87North – it’s undeniable. They have really found a way to tap into mainstream culture and audiences in a way that very few filmmakers do. They have their finger on the pulse of the culture and what audiences respond to.”
How To Rob A Bank follows a crew that begins carrying out audacious bank robberies while livestreaming its crimes. As their exploits attract attention and the robbers gain online fame, a veteran FBI agent joins forces with a brilliant software engineer to track them down. The crew, however, continues to raise the stakes as it prepares for its biggest heist yet.
Directed by David Leitch and written by Mark Biancull, the film features Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Christian Slater as Walton, Pete Davidson and John C. Reilly.
Produced by Amazon MGM Studios, How To Rob A Bank will be released in cinemas on November 20, with Sony Pictures Releasing International handling its theatrical release.

President Trump called Jensen Huang on Tuesday, before the Nvidia chief stepped down amid a rapidly unfolding spy scandal, and urged him to keep fighting for his job, according to two people briefed on the conversation.

By the age of 23, he had signed a professional contract with Nike and represented Great Britain on the global stage.
But at the same time, his body was deteriorating - enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat.
Balancing an intense training regime with disordered eating meant the 28-year-old returned from a running camp in Uganda weighing just eight stone (51kg) at 5ft 5in (1.7m). He had such brittle bones that he was told his career could be over.
After suffering two stress fractures in the space of four months, Smith sought professional help and was diagnosed with REDs – relative energy deficiency in sport.
It is a syndrome that can affect anyone and if left undiagnosed or untreated, can have an impact on performance and cause serious, long-lasting health problems.
The symptoms are slightly better documented in women - just last month, tennis player Emma Navarro revealed her diagnosis and subsequent decision to step away from competition until 2027.
But men are just as susceptible and due to stigma and lack of obvious warning signs, it can go undetected for longer and means many, like Smith, suffer in silence.
BBC Sport explains what the condition is, how it affects men and women and why, despite its prevalence and severity, REDs remains a relatively under-reported and overlooked area of sports science.
REDs can cause bone stress injuries, disrupted sleep, fatigue and low mood. Left untreated, the condition can lead to serious long-term health problems, including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease and fertility issues.
Dr Nicky Keay, an expert in hormone health, says many of these symptoms stem from hormonal disruption caused by insufficient energy intake.
"Hormones go to every single bit in your body. So, if your hormones are not working well for you, you're going to feel it in all sorts of different areas," she says.
"In order to have healthy hormones, they need to be fed regularly. If you're not doing that and there's an energy deficit, often some of those hormone systems will slow down or shut down completely."
Women have a monthly barometer of their hormone health with the menstrual cycle, described by Keay as a "free monthly medical check".
Put simply, she says, a woman suffering from REDs has her periods "switched off".
For men, it is more subtle – testosterone levels will drop, resulting in a reduced libido and fatigue.
The impact on a woman's period is why the condition was first referred to in the early 1990s as the "female athlete triad".
But it was renamed by the International Olympic Committee in 2014 to acknowledge the broader range of symptoms of energy deficiency and that it also harms male athletes.
"We realised we were ignoring the other half of the population," Keay says.
"It's a strange situation because normally it's women's health that is the one being ignored but, in this situation, it's the men who weren't being recognised or represented."
Twelve years later that decision appears to be vindicated, with recent research highlighting the prevalence in men.
Meta-analysis published in Australian journal Sports Medicine last year, following a study involving thousands of elite and amateur athletes around the world, indicated 44.2% of female athletes and 49.4% of male athletes had low energy availability.
So why is REDs so common?
One of the answers lies in the phrase 'lighter is faster'.
For decades, it had been an accepted wisdom in sports like endurance running, cycling, climbing, horse riding, dancing and aesthetic sports like diving and gymnastics.
And for athletes like Smith, it is how his problems started.
"I believed it for years. I thought that was the way forward," he says.
"I started thinking 'how do I improve my half marathon by 10 seconds? Is it a drop in weight?'. And that's when my head completely went."
Initially, the strategy can work.
When it comes to choosing energy to cover training demand or energy to stay healthy, the body has learned through evolution and threat of predators to always prioritise movement.
It means that athletes can drop weight and still train and exercise and achieve good results.
But eventually, the luck runs out.
Described by Keay as "fool's gold", the body will adjust to the energy deficit and cause a drop in performance and high risk of injuries.
Olympic and world champion Jonny Brownlee acknowledges under-fuelling mistakes he made in his triathlon career contributed to serious injuries.
"I didn't see the importance of it. Training came first and I think we weren't educated enough in how important fuelling was," he tells BBC Sport.
"You were seen, culturally, as a bit weak if you were fuelling on the bike. And the impact of that was definitely injuries - probably not recovering from my training quite as well as I should have done, stress responses, stress fractures. So there's that side of it and probably underperformance in races as well."
Brownlee, who recently announced his retirement, believes the culture of not fuelling on the bike has now changed but a stigma lingers around REDs and the perception that it is a "female issue".
"In females, there are more obvious signs but in males it can go under the radar a little bit and then it hits you by a really serious injury," he says.
"I think there's a stigma attached in there, or it's not looked at as the obvious answer to some of your problems, it's found later down the line. Men also don't like to talk about under-fuelling because it's just seen as 'you probably should feel better and you should be on top of that'."
It is those attitudes among male athletes that prompted Keay to conduct an experiment in 2019.
Assessing 50 male competitive cyclists, Keay found in her initial screenings that nearly half had poor bone health and 25% were suffering from REDs.
The cyclists were then split into two groups and across a six-month period, one half continued their training and fuelling habits as before while the others were tutored by Keay and offered nutrition and training advice.
"The group that I left to their own devices unfortunately went on the default and they lost even more bone mineral density, similar to an astronaut in space… And they performed OK, but relative to their functional threshold power, they didn't get the race results that you would have expected.
"For the group I took under my wing, there was an improvement in their bone health and really good race results.
"So, I had evidence that REDs definitely does exist quite extensively in my group of the male cyclists and you're going to underperform if you don't fuel sufficiently. The good news is that REDs is reversible. But if you don't take action, it's a decline."
As the syndrome and its symptoms are still not commonly known, it is often difficult to know where to find help.
After former GB runner Pippa Woolven's struggles with the condition, she set up a website called Project REDs which offers information and practical resources for athletes, coaches, parents and healthcare professionals.
Keay also helps people competing at all levels to recover from REDs. Most of her patients are women, but she is starting to see more men reach out for help who, she says, are often in "bad shape".
"I think the men are maybe more reluctant than the women, or maybe they don't realise they've got it. Sometimes they might use a different word for it, they say burnout," Keay says.
"I don't mind that though because there is definitely a psychological aspect to REDs. Why are you doing this? Why are you not eating the carbohydrates?"
Sometimes, it's hard to answer those questions because the under-fuelling is unintentional, either from not understanding or underestimating energy requirements or failing to match an increase in the intensity or duration of exercise with higher calorie or carbohydrate intake.
For others, former British cycling champion Brian Smith among them, the answer comes from intention.
Competing in the road race for Great Britain at the 1996 Olympics should have been the highlight of his career but, behind the scenes of the success, Smith was suffering with an eating disorder and serious mental health condition called bulimia – something he believes he developed from his sport's obsession with weight.
"I always felt like I was overweight. Everybody was under pressure regarding weight, but nobody really spoke about it," he says.
"I'm just under six foot and I've got large glutes and thigh muscles. As a road cyclist, I used to race at 68kg and for my height and build, that's quite skinny. I even got down to about 66kg and when I got down to that, I felt underpowered, I felt bad."
Smith, now 59, only discovered he had been suffering from REDs during his career when he started running eight years ago and developed three severe stress fractures, including one in his femur.
Such has been the toll on his body that Smith says he would now never encourage anyone to pursue a career as a professional cyclist.
"It really is not healthy," he says. "If you want to go to the highest levels of the sport, you will suffer later on in life. You're destroying your body.
"Sporting teams don't care - all they're worried about is performance. So they will nurture a rider, they will feed a rider, they'll get a rider to be a certain weight. They don't care about what happens to them later in life.
"I'm suffering now and I've so many regrets. I just wish I'd known more about this."
While Smith believes his sport has a long way to go in changing attitudes, British Cycling says a lot of progress has been made through education that starts at academy level and annual physical and psychological screenings.
"One of the big things we've done in the past 10 years is try and turn this into a performance-related conversation," Dr Nigel Jones, British Cycling chief medical officer, tells BBC Sport.
"Now, we couch the conversation with an athlete around 'if you under-fuel, you will not be able to perform at your best', whereas previously, conversations in power-to-weight ratio sports might have been 'you need to be lighter'.
"I think it would be naive to say REDs is never going to be an issue. But I would like to believe that its prevalence will reduce with the work that we're doing," he adds.
British Cycling is not alone in this approach, with World Climbing taking things a step further two years ago with the introduction of mandatory health checks on athletes.
Using a combination of pre-season questionnaires and 'random and targeted' screenings at competitions - similar to the way doping tests are enforced – climbers at World Championship or World Cup-level competitions are monitored for any indicators of low energy availability or REDs and could be prevented from competing if they are not deemed to be healthy.
The policy was drawn up by expert Professor Naama Constantini, who says she is "proud" of the move by World Climbing and believes other federations should follow suit.
"We are trying to educate and prevent. I'm not a policeman and we're not looking for cheaters. I'm a medical doctor and we want to make sure our athletes are healthy," she says.
"Prevention is the best medicine you can give. We want athletes and coaches to understand that it's not about weight. It's about strength, it's about performance and fuelling the body and you pay a price if you lose weight in an unhealthy way."
With more awareness and education, it is hoped the tide can be turned on REDs.
But many still suffer in ignorance, as well as silence. That is what motivates Jake Smith to keep sharing his recovery on social media, with hundreds of men and women messaging him for advice and support.
Smith has managed to reverse his condition and is now racing better than ever, recently completing the Berlin marathon in a personal-best time of two hours, nine minutes and 24 seconds.
The big goal is the 2028 Olympics, but he is adamant that the priority is making sure he stands on every start line as healthy as possible.
"I'd never want to see an athlete go through the years I've had. I'm 10-15 kilos heavier than I've ever been and the biggest thing I can say is I've never been so happy. You need a healthy body to do everything else.
"I'm heavier, I'm faster, I'm happier."

Eight people have tested positive for Shigella infection in Malappuram district, with five cases linked to a wedding feast at Korakkuthu in Elamkulam panchayat near Perinthalmanna.
The outbreak has prompted the Health department to step up surveillance and preventive measures in the area.
The five patients attended a wedding held on October 31, 2026, in ward 12 of Elamkulam panchayat. Around 80 people who attended the function have since reported symptoms of diarrhoea. A child from the area is also suspected to have Shigella infection and is under special observation.
The other confirmed cases include a four-year-old girl who ate food from a snack shop at 5th Mile at Amarambalam near Nilambur, and two people who ate mandi rice from a restaurant at Palunda near Chungathara, Nilambur.
The girl and the two patients from Chungathara are undergoing treatment at Government District Hospital, Nilambur. Several others, including the girl’s mother, have also reported similar symptoms.
The Food Safety department has collected samples of food and drinking water served at the wedding and sent them for testing. Stool samples of those affected will be examined at the laboratory at Government Medical College, Manjeri.
A special health team has begun surveillance and field-level interventions. The Health department has advised people to drink boiled and cooled water and eat properly cooked food. Drinking water sources should also be superchlorinated using bleaching powder, said health officials.
The health authorities, in coordination with the panchayat, will intensify inspections at local establishments and public functions. Event organisers have been asked to follow public health guidelines.
